`src/templates/sv/msix/pcileech_msix_bar_router.sv`:

```sv
//
// PCILeech MSI-X BAR router (MX-04)
//
// Sits in the served BAR's slot of pcileech_tlps128_bar_controller. Each DWORD
// read or write has exactly one owner: the MSI-X table window, the PBA window,
// or the BAR's register implementation ("inner"). Windows come from the
// validated donor layout (src/device_clone/msix_layout.py, decode_parameters):
// inclusive first/last byte offsets bounded by the real vector count, so
// padded entries of the power-of-two core are never reachable.
//
// Capacity: the BAR engines issue at most one read and one write per clock and
// cannot be stalled. Both owners accept one of each per clock and answer reads
// exactly two clocks later (pcileech_bar_impl_device and
// pcileech_bar_impl_zerowrite4k do too), so responses leave in request order
// and never collide. On reset the router drops in-flight MSI-X reads, as
// pcileech_bar_impl_device does; zerowrite4k still answers reads issued during
// reset. A read and a write of one DWORD in the same clock have no defined
// order from the engines: the MSI-X core returns the new bytes,
// pcileech_bar_impl_device returns the old ones. A latency mismatch is a design error and stops simulation.
//

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

module pcileech_msix_bar_router #(
    parameter [32:0] BAR_SIZE = 4096,    // power of two up to 4 GiB, as the inner implementation's BAR_SIZE
    parameter IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH = 1,
    parameter [31:0] TABLE_FIRST = 32'h0,
    parameter [31:0] TABLE_LAST = 32'hF,
    parameter [31:0] PBA_FIRST = 32'h800,
    parameter [31:0] PBA_LAST = 32'h807
)(
    input               rst,
    input               clk,
    // from the BAR controller
    input [31:0]        wr_addr,
    input [3:0]         wr_be,
    input [31:0]        wr_data,
    input               wr_valid,
    input [87:0]        rd_req_ctx,
    input [31:0]        rd_req_addr,
    input               rd_req_valid,
    output [87:0]       rd_rsp_ctx,
    output [31:0]       rd_rsp_data,
    output              rd_rsp_valid,
    // to the inner register implementation (address/data buses are shared)
    output              inner_wr_valid,
    output              inner_rd_req_valid,
    input [87:0]        inner_rd_rsp_ctx,
    input [31:0]        inner_rd_rsp_data,
    input               inner_rd_rsp_valid,
    // to the MSI-X core host port
    output                       host_wr_valid,
    output                       host_wr_pba,
    output [IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH+1:0] host_wr_dw,
    output [31:0]                host_wr_data,
    output [3:0]                 host_wr_be,
    output                       host_rd_valid,
    output                       host_rd_pba,
    output [IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH+1:0] host_rd_dw,
    input [31:0]                 host_rd_data
);
    localparam [32:0] BAR_LAST = BAR_SIZE - 33'd1;
    localparam [31:0] OFFSET_MASK = BAR_LAST[31:0] & 32'hFFFFFFFC;

    wire [31:0] wr_off = wr_addr & OFFSET_MASK;
    wire [31:0] rd_off = rd_req_addr & OFFSET_MASK;

    wire wr_tbl = (wr_off >= TABLE_FIRST) && (wr_off <= TABLE_LAST);
    wire wr_pba = (wr_off >= PBA_FIRST) && (wr_off <= PBA_LAST);
    wire rd_tbl = (rd_off >= TABLE_FIRST) && (rd_off <= TABLE_LAST);
    wire rd_pba = (rd_off >= PBA_FIRST) && (rd_off <= PBA_LAST);

    wire [31:0] wr_rel = wr_off - (wr_pba ? PBA_FIRST : TABLE_FIRST);
    wire [31:0] rd_rel = rd_off - (rd_pba ? PBA_FIRST : TABLE_FIRST);

    assign inner_wr_valid     = wr_valid && !wr_tbl && !wr_pba;
    assign inner_rd_req_valid = rd_req_valid && !rd_tbl && !rd_pba;

    // PBA writes reach the core, which ignores them (no other owner may answer).
    assign host_wr_valid = wr_valid && (wr_tbl || wr_pba);
    assign host_wr_pba   = wr_pba;
    assign host_wr_dw    = wr_rel[IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH+3:2];
    assign host_wr_data  = wr_data;
    assign host_wr_be    = wr_be;
    assign host_rd_valid = rd_req_valid && (rd_tbl || rd_pba);
    assign host_rd_pba   = rd_pba;
    assign host_rd_dw    = rd_rel[IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH+3:2];

    // Carry the context of MSI-X reads alongside the core's two-clock latency.
    reg [87:0] msix_ctx_d1, msix_ctx_d2;
    reg        msix_rd_d1, msix_rd_d2;
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            msix_rd_d1 <= 1'b0;
            msix_rd_d2 <= 1'b0;
        end
        else begin
            msix_rd_d1 <= host_rd_valid;
            msix_rd_d2 <= msix_rd_d1;
        end
        msix_ctx_d1 <= rd_req_ctx;
        msix_ctx_d2 <= msix_ctx_d1;
    end

    assign rd_rsp_valid = msix_rd_d2 || inner_rd_rsp_valid;
    assign rd_rsp_ctx   = msix_rd_d2 ? msix_ctx_d2 : inner_rd_rsp_ctx;
    assign rd_rsp_data  = msix_rd_d2 ? host_rd_data : inner_rd_rsp_data;

`ifndef SYNTHESIS
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (!rst && msix_rd_d2 && inner_rd_rsp_valid)
            $fatal(1, "pcileech_msix_bar_router: inner and MSI-X responses collided (latency mismatch)");
`endif
endmodule

```

`src/templates/sv/msix/pcileech_msix_tlp_tx.sv`:

```sv
//
// PCILeech FPGA - MSI-X message transmit (MX-06)
//
// Packs one MSI-X Memory Write from the vendored pcie_msix core into the
// PCILeech 128-bit TLP stream and merges it with the BAR completion stream
// (pcileech_tlps128_bar_rdengine output), so both leave on the BAR
// controller's single tlps_out input to pcileech_tlps128_sink_mux1.
//
// Stream protocol (from the consumers, pcileech_tlps128_sink_mux1 and
// pcileech_tlps128_dst64): a source behaves like a standard FIFO with a valid
// flag. tready in clock T requests one beat; the beat is presented with tvalid
// in clock T+1 and is consumed unconditionally. has_data means at least one
// whole packet is available. The mux locks onto a source once it sees has_data
// and releases it only on a beat with tlast, so once has_data is raised the
// packet must be delivered: a committed message cannot be withdrawn.
//
// Lane order (from pcileech_tlps128_dst64 and the BAR engines): DW n of a TLP
// is tdata[32*n +: 32] in PCIe bit order (fmt at [31:29]). Payload DWs carry
// byte 0 in [31:24], so the little-endian Message Data is byte swapped, as the
// read engine swaps completion data.
//
// Arbitration: at each packet boundary a committed message goes before a BAR
// completion. A BAR completion produced after a message was committed (a PBA
// read, for example) therefore never passes it (PCIe ordering: completions
// must not pass posted requests). Configuration completions use another
// upstream mux input with higher priority; they never show interrupt state.
// A new message is accepted only when the buffer is empty, which is never true
// at the boundary that ends a message, so a waiting completion always goes
// next: neither stream can starve the other.
//
// msg_ready is high whenever the one-message buffer is empty and msg_allow is
// high, so the core's presented message is committed in its first WAIT_TLP
// clock unless the previous message is still waiting for the stream.
//
// msg_allow must be the live (unregistered) send condition: MSI-X Enable,
// function unmasked, Bus Master Enable, and no msix_clear. The core sees those
// one clock late, so without this gate a message could be committed in the
// clock a clear arrives or just after bus mastering is turned off. Gating
// ready (not valid) keeps both sides in step: no handshake, no send, and the
// core then withdraws and re-pends or drops the message itself.
//
// A message already committed cannot be withdrawn (see has_data above), so it
// is sent even if the controls drop while it waits for the stream. For a
// clear (FLR and the other PCIe resets) the merger instead drains it first:
// clear_out, which drives the core's msix_clear, stays high until the buffer
// is empty. The core holds its sweep at the start while msix_clear is high and
// drops host table writes until the sweep ends, so a message from before the
// clear always leaves before any new table entry can be programmed. rst
// (which includes link down and hot reset) discards the buffer.
//

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

module pcileech_msix_tlp_tx (
    input               clk,
    input               rst,
    // from pcie_msix (TLP_HDR_WIDTH = 128, verilog-pcie header layout:
    // hdr[127:96] = DW0, hdr[95:64] = DW1, hdr[63:32] = DW2, hdr[31:0] = DW3)
    input  [127:0]      msg_hdr,
    input  [31:0]       msg_data,
    input               msg_valid,
    input               msg_allow,
    output              msg_ready,
    // PCIe-defined reset request in, held clear for the core out
    input               clear_req,
    output              clear_out,
    // completion stream source (pull, read latency 1)
    input  [127:0]      cpl_tdata,
    input  [3:0]        cpl_tkeepdw,
    input               cpl_tlast,
    input  [8:0]        cpl_tuser,
    input               cpl_tvalid,
    input               cpl_has_data,
    output              cpl_tready,
    // merged stream (same protocol)
    output [127:0]      out_tdata,
    output [3:0]        out_tkeepdw,
    output              out_tlast,
    output [8:0]        out_tuser,
    output              out_tvalid,
    output              out_has_data,
    input               out_tready
);

    localparam [1:0] SEL_NONE = 2'd0, SEL_MSG = 2'd1, SEL_CPL = 2'd2;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // One-message buffer: up to two beats (4DW header + 1 payload DW).
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg [127:0] beat0, beat1;
    reg         two_beats;
    reg [1:0]   msg_beats = 2'd0;   // beats not yet pulled
    reg         msg_next_is_1;      // the next beat to pull is beat1

    wire [31:0] data_bs = { msg_data[7:0], msg_data[15:8], msg_data[23:16], msg_data[31:24] };
    wire        hdr_4dw = msg_hdr[125];  // fmt[0]: 4DW header

    assign msg_ready = (msg_beats == 2'd0) && msg_allow && !rst;
    wire   msg_commit = msg_valid && msg_ready;
    wire   msg_has = msg_beats != 2'd0;

    reg    clear_pending = 1'b0;
    assign clear_out = clear_req || (clear_pending && msg_has);

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Packet-boundary arbitration (locked until the beat with tlast)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    reg  [1:0]  sel = SEL_NONE;
    reg [127:0] o_tdata = 128'd0;
    reg [3:0]   o_tkeepdw = 4'd0;
    reg         o_tlast = 1'b0;
    reg         o_first = 1'b0;
    reg         o_valid = 1'b0;

    assign out_tvalid  = (sel == SEL_CPL) ? cpl_tvalid  : (sel == SEL_MSG) ? o_valid : 1'b0;
    assign out_tdata   = (sel == SEL_CPL) ? cpl_tdata   : (sel == SEL_MSG) ? o_tdata : 128'd0;
    assign out_tkeepdw = (sel == SEL_CPL) ? cpl_tkeepdw : (sel == SEL_MSG) ? o_tkeepdw : 4'd0;
    assign out_tlast   = (sel == SEL_CPL) ? cpl_tlast   : (sel == SEL_MSG) ? o_tlast : 1'b0;
    assign out_tuser   = (sel == SEL_CPL) ? cpl_tuser   :
                         (sel == SEL_MSG) ? { 7'd0, o_tlast, o_first } : 9'd0;

    wire [1:0] sel_new  = msg_has ? SEL_MSG : (cpl_has_data ? SEL_CPL : SEL_NONE);
    wire [1:0] sel_next = ((sel == SEL_NONE) || (out_tvalid && out_tlast)) ? sel_new : sel;

    wire msg_pull     = out_tready && (sel_next == SEL_MSG) && msg_has;
    assign cpl_tready = out_tready && (sel_next == SEL_CPL);
    assign out_has_data = msg_has || cpl_has_data;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            clear_pending <= clear_req;
            msg_beats <= 2'd0;
            sel       <= SEL_NONE;
            o_valid   <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            sel     <= sel_next;
            o_valid <= msg_pull;
            clear_pending <= clear_req || (clear_pending && msg_has);
            if (msg_pull) begin
                o_tdata   <= msg_next_is_1 ? beat1 : beat0;
                o_tkeepdw <= msg_next_is_1 ? 4'b0001 : 4'b1111;
                o_tlast   <= msg_next_is_1 || !two_beats;
                o_first   <= !msg_next_is_1;
                msg_beats <= msg_beats - 2'd1;
                msg_next_is_1 <= 1'b1;
            end
            if (msg_commit) begin
                two_beats     <= hdr_4dw;
                msg_beats     <= hdr_4dw ? 2'd2 : 2'd1;
                msg_next_is_1 <= 1'b0;
                if (hdr_4dw) begin
                    beat0 <= { msg_hdr[31:0], msg_hdr[63:32], msg_hdr[95:64], msg_hdr[127:96] };
                    beat1 <= { 96'd0, data_bs };
                end else begin
                    beat0 <= { data_bs, msg_hdr[63:32], msg_hdr[95:64], msg_hdr[127:96] };
                    beat1 <= 128'd0;
                end
            end
        end
    end

`ifndef SYNTHESIS
    // A commit can only happen with an empty buffer, so it never overlaps a pull.
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (!rst && msg_commit && msg_pull) $fatal(1, "msix_tlp_tx: commit overlapped a pull");
        // A completion beat arrives only in response to cpl_tready, which is
        // given only to the selected source; anything else would be dropped.
        if (!rst && cpl_tvalid && sel != SEL_CPL) $fatal(1, "msix_tlp_tx: completion beat while not selected");
    end
`endif

endmodule

```

`src/templates/sv/pcileech_bar_impl_device.sv.j2`:

{# Validate before formatting any value or emitting storage. #}
{% set readonly_fallback = bar_model_readonly_fallback | default(false) %}
{% if not bar_model %}
{{ throw_error('Device BAR implementation requires a nonempty learned register model or the read-only fallback') }}
{% endif %}
{% if not bar_model.registers and not readonly_fallback %}
{{ throw_error('Device BAR implementation requires a nonempty learned register model or the read-only fallback') }}
{% endif %}
{# Context compatibility may stringify integer dictionary keys. #}
{% set registers = {} %}
{% for offset, reg in bar_model.registers.items() %}
{% if int(offset) in registers %}{{ throw_error('Duplicate BAR register offset') }}{% endif %}
{% set ignored = registers.update({int(offset): reg}) %}
{% endfor %}
{% set layout = namespace(end=0, dwords={}) %}
{% for offset, reg in registers.items() | sort %}
{% if reg.reset is none %}
{{ throw_error('BAR register 0x%X has no initial value: %s' % (offset, reg.hints.get('initial_value_absent_reason', 'reason missing'))) }}
{% endif %}
{% if reg.width not in [1, 2, 4] or offset < 0 or offset % reg.width or offset < layout.end or offset + reg.width > bar_model.size %}
{{ throw_error('Invalid or overlapping BAR register layout at 0x%X' % offset) }}
{% endif %}

{% if reg.reset < 0 or reg.reset > full_mask or reg.rw_mask < 0 or reg.rw_mask > full_mask %}
{{ throw_error('BAR register value or mask exceeds width at 0x%X' % offset) }}
{% endif %}
{% set layout.end = offset + reg.width %}
{% set ignored = layout.dwords.setdefault((offset // 4) * 4, []).append((offset, reg)) %}
{% endfor %}

//
// Device-Specific PCILeech BAR Storage Implementation
// Auto-generated for {{ device_signature }}.
{% if readonly_fallback %}
// READ-ONLY FALLBACK: no learned register model exists for this BAR. Every read
// returns zero and every write is ignored across the whole aperture. This is
// not donor behavior; it claims nothing the evidence does not show.
{% endif %}
// Plain RW masks grant storage updates only. Other semantics are unsupported.
// Unmapped read lanes return zero as an approximation, not a donor measurement.
// Register Map Summary:
{% for offset, reg in registers.items() | sort %}
{% set evidence = reg.hints.get('evidence') or {} %}
{% set source = evidence.get('initial_value_source') or 'legacy_unverified' %}
{% set provenance = 'legacy_unverified' if 'maybe_rw1c' in reg.hints or not evidence.get('classifications') else 'evidence_backed' %}
//   0x{{ '%04X' % offset }}: {{ 'DWORD' if reg.width == 4 else ('WORD' if reg.width == 2 else 'BYTE') }} {{ 'RW' if reg.rw_mask else 'RO storage' }} (initial=0x{{ '%0*X' % (reg.width * 2, reg.reset) }}, source={{ source | replace('\n', ' ') | replace('\r', ' ') | replace('\\', '/') }}, unknown_mask=0x{{ '%0*X' % (reg.width * 2, reg.hints.get('unknown_mask', 2 ** (reg.width * 8) - 1)) }}, provenance={{ provenance }})
{% endfor %}
// FPGA reset initializes storage from the recorded initial value; it does not
// establish the donor's reset behavior. Unsupported actions are not emulated.

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

module {{ device_bar_impl_module | default('pcileech_bar_impl_device') }} #(
    parameter BAR_SIZE = {{ bar_model.size }}
)(
    input               rst,
    input               clk,
    input [31:0]        wr_addr,
    input [31:0]        wr_data,
    input [3:0]         wr_be,
    input               wr_valid,
    input [87:0]        rd_req_ctx,
    input [31:0]        rd_req_addr,
    input               rd_req_valid,
    output reg [87:0]   rd_rsp_ctx,
    output reg [31:0]   rd_rsp_data,
    output reg          rd_rsp_valid
    {% if interrupt_config and interrupt_config.strategy in ['msi', 'msix'] %}
    , output wire       interrupt_assert
    , output wire [7:0] interrupt_data
    {% endif %}
);
    // The controller passes host addresses (TLP address / upper request bits),
    // not BAR offsets. Decode only the offset within this power-of-two BAR.
    {% set bar_size = bar_model.size | int %}
    {% set pow2 = namespace(ok=false) %}
    {% for bit in range(2, 33) %}{% if 2 ** bit == bar_size %}{% set pow2.ok = true %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}
    {% if not pow2.ok %}{{ throw_error('BAR size 0x%X is not a power of two between 4 bytes and 4 GiB' % bar_size) }}{% endif %}
    localparam [31:0] OFFSET_MASK = 32'h{{ '%08X' % (((bar_size - 1) // 4) * 4) }};
    wire [31:0] wr_offset = wr_addr & OFFSET_MASK;
    wire [31:0] rd_offset = rd_req_addr & OFFSET_MASK;

    {% for offset, reg in registers.items() | sort %}
    reg [{{ reg.width * 8 - 1 }}:0] reg_0x{{ '%04X' % offset }};
    {% endfor %}

    // Reset and plain storage writes have one owner. Each DWORD is decoded once.
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            {% for offset, reg in registers.items() | sort %}
            reg_0x{{ '%04X' % offset }} <= {{ reg.width * 8 }}'h{{ '%0*X' % (reg.width * 2, reg.reset) }};
            {% endfor %}
        end
        else if (wr_valid) begin
            case (wr_offset)
                {% for aligned_offset, regs in layout.dwords.items() | sort %}
                {% set writable = namespace(any=false) %}
                {% for offset, reg in regs %}
                {% if reg.rw_mask %}{% set writable.any = true %}{% endif %}
                {% endfor %}
                {% if writable.any %}
                32'h{{ '%08X' % aligned_offset }}: begin
                    {% for offset, reg in regs %}
                    {% set reg_name = 'reg_0x%04X' % offset %}
                    {% for byte in range(reg.width) %}
                    {% set mask = (reg.rw_mask // (2 ** (8 * byte))) % 256 %}
                    {% set lane = offset % 4 + byte %}
                    {% if mask %}
                    if (wr_be[{{ lane }}]) {{ reg_name }}[{{ byte * 8 + 7 }}:{{ byte * 8 }}] <= ({{ reg_name }}[{{ byte * 8 + 7 }}:{{ byte * 8 }}] & ~8'h{{ '%02X' % mask }}) | (wr_data[{{ lane * 8 + 7 }}:{{ lane * 8 }}] & 8'h{{ '%02X' % mask }});
                    {% endif %}
                    {% endfor %}
                    {% endfor %}
                end
                {% endif %}
                {% endfor %}
                default: begin
                    // Unregistered writes have no effect.
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

    // Two-cycle read response, composing all registers sharing a DWORD.
    reg [87:0] rd_req_ctx_d1;
    reg        rd_req_valid_d1;
    reg [31:0] rd_data_d1;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            rd_req_ctx_d1 <= 88'd0;
            rd_req_valid_d1 <= 1'b0;
            rd_data_d1 <= 32'd0;
        end
        else begin
            rd_req_ctx_d1 <= rd_req_ctx;
            rd_req_valid_d1 <= rd_req_valid;
            rd_data_d1 <= 32'd0;
            if (rd_req_valid) begin
                case (rd_offset)
                    {% for aligned_offset, regs in layout.dwords.items() | sort %}
                    32'h{{ '%08X' % aligned_offset }}: begin
                        {% for offset, reg in regs %}
                        rd_data_d1[{{ (offset % 4 + reg.width) * 8 - 1 }}:{{ (offset % 4) * 8 }}] <= reg_0x{{ '%04X' % offset }};
                        {% endfor %}
                    end
                    {% endfor %}
                    default: begin
                        // Unmapped reads return zero; no semantics are inferred.
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            rd_rsp_ctx <= 88'd0;
            rd_rsp_valid <= 1'b0;
            rd_rsp_data <= 32'd0;
        end
        else begin
            rd_rsp_ctx <= rd_req_ctx_d1;
            rd_rsp_valid <= rd_req_valid_d1;
            rd_rsp_data <= rd_data_d1;
        end
    end

    {% if interrupt_config and interrupt_config.strategy in ['msi', 'msix'] %}
    // No supported device interrupt contract: keep the optional outputs inactive.
    assign interrupt_assert = 1'b0;
    assign interrupt_data = 8'h00;
    {% endif %}
endmodule

module pcileech_tlps128_bar_controller(
    input                   rst,
    input                   clk,
    input                   bar_en,
    input [15:0]            pcie_id,
    IfPCIeSignals.mpro      pcie_ctx,       // read-only PCIe core status (clk domain)
    input                   rst_pcie_user,  // PCIe core user reset: PERST, link down
    IfAXIS128.sink_lite     tlps_in,
    IfAXIS128.source        tlps_out
);
{% set _msix = msix_rtl if (msix_rtl is defined and msix_rtl) else none %}
    
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1: TLP RECEIVE:
    // Receive incoming BAR requests from the TLP stream:
    // send them onwards to read and write FIFOs
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    wire in_is_wr_ready;
    bit  in_is_wr_last;
    wire in_is_first    = tlps_in.tuser[0];
    wire in_is_bar      = bar_en && (tlps_in.tuser[8:2] != 0);
    wire in_is_rd       = (in_is_first && tlps_in.tlast && ((tlps_in.tdata[31:25] == 7'b0000000) || (tlps_in.tdata[31:25] == 7'b0010000) || (tlps_in.tdata[31:24] == 8'b00000010)));
    wire in_is_wr       = in_is_wr_last || (in_is_first && in_is_wr_ready && ((tlps_in.tdata[31:25] == 7'b0100000) || (tlps_in.tdata[31:25] == 7'b0110000) || (tlps_in.tdata[31:24] == 8'b01000010)));
    
    always @ ( posedge clk )
        if ( rst ) begin
            in_is_wr_last <= 0;
        end
        else if ( tlps_in.tvalid ) begin
            in_is_wr_last <= !tlps_in.tlast && in_is_wr;
        end
    
    wire [6:0]  wr_bar;
    wire [31:0] wr_addr;
    wire [3:0]  wr_be;
    wire [31:0] wr_data;
    wire        wr_valid;
    wire [87:0] rd_req_ctx;
    wire [6:0]  rd_req_bar;
    wire [31:0] rd_req_addr;
    wire        rd_req_valid;
    wire [87:0] rd_rsp_ctx;
    wire [31:0] rd_rsp_data;
    wire        rd_rsp_valid;

    // way to tlps_out.
    IfAXIS128 tlps_bar_cpl();
{% endif %}

        .rst            ( rst                           ),
        .clk            ( clk                           ),

        .tlps_out       ( {{ 'tlps_bar_cpl.source' if _msix else 'tlps_out' }}{{ ' ' * (31 - ('tlps_bar_cpl.source' if _msix else 'tlps_out')|length) }}),

        .rd_req_ctx     ( rd_req_ctx                    ),
        .rd_req_bar     ( rd_req_bar                    ),

        .rd_rsp_ctx     ( rd_rsp_ctx                    ),

    );

    pcileech_tlps128_bar_wrengine i_pcileech_tlps128_bar_wrengine(
        .rst            ( rst                           ),
        .clk            ( clk                           ),
        // TLPs:
        .tlps_in        ( tlps_in                       ),

        .wr_addr        ( wr_addr                       ),
        .wr_be          ( wr_be                         ),
        .wr_data        ( wr_data                       ),
        .wr_valid       ( wr_valid                      )
    );

    wire [31:0] bar_rsp_data[7];
    wire        bar_rsp_valid[7];
    
{% if timing_config is defined and timing_config and timing_config.get('enable_latency_jitter', False) %}

{#
    Gap C — donor-BAR-index serving. The donor's primary register window is
    served at its REAL PCI BAR index (served_bar_index); every other slot is a
    non-responding stub (pcileech_bar_impl_none), with loopaddr kept at slot 1
    when free for test/diagnostics. A 64-bit served BAR lights two adjacent hit
    bits (N and N+1), so slot N+1 MUST be `none` — never loopaddr — or the
    response mux would be double-driven. When served_bar_index == 0 and 32-bit
    this reproduces the historical wiring (device@0, loopaddr@1, none@2..6).

{% set _models = (bar_config.get('bar_models') if bar_config else none) or {} %}
{% set _served_model = _models.get(_served) or _models.get(_served | string) %}
{% set _regs = (_served_model.get('regs') or _served_model.get('registers')) if _served_model else none %}
{% set _has_model = (_regs.keys() | list | length > 0) if _regs else false %}
{% endif %}
{% set _bar_size = (bar_config.aperture_size | default(4096)) if bar_config else 4096 %}
{% macro bar_inst(module, k, inst, param_size=None, wr_valid=None, rd_valid=None, rsp=None) -%}
{% set _wr_valid = wr_valid or ('wr_valid && wr_bar[' ~ k ~ ']') %}
{% set _rd_valid = rd_valid or ('rd_req_valid && rd_req_bar[' ~ k ~ ']') %}
{% set _rsp = rsp or ['bar_rsp_ctx[' ~ k ~ ']', 'bar_rsp_data[' ~ k ~ ']', 'bar_rsp_valid[' ~ k ~ ']'] %}
{% if param_size is not none %}    {{ module }} #(
        .BAR_SIZE       ( {{ param_size }} )
    ) {{ inst }}(
{% else %}    {{ module }} {{ inst }}(
{% endif %}        .rst            ( rst                           ),
        .clk            ( clk                           ),
        .wr_addr        ( wr_addr                       ),
        .wr_be          ( wr_be                         ),
        .wr_data        ( wr_data                       ),
        .wr_valid       ( {{ _wr_valid }} ),
        .rd_req_ctx     ( rd_req_ctx                    ),
        .rd_req_addr    ( rd_req_addr                   ),
        .rd_req_valid   ( {{ _rd_valid }} ),
        .rd_rsp_ctx     ( {{ _rsp[0] }} ),
        .rd_rsp_data    ( {{ _rsp[1] }} ),
        .rd_rsp_valid   ( {{ _rsp[2] }} )
    );
{%- endmacro %}
    // ========================================================================
    // BAR implementations (served register window at BAR index {{ _served }})
    // ========================================================================
{% if device_bar_slots is defined %}
{% if _msix and ((_msix.bar_index | string) not in device_bar_slots or device_bar_slots.get(_msix.bar_index | string).size != _msix.bar_size) %}
{% error "MSI-X layout disagrees with its served BAR descriptor" %}
{% endif %}
{% set _upper_slots = [] %}
{% for slot in device_bar_slots.values() %}
{% if slot.is_64bit %}{% set ignored = _upper_slots.append(slot.index + 1) %}{% endif %}
{% endfor %}
{% for k in range(7) %}
{% set _slot = device_bar_slots.get(k | string) %}
{% if _slot %}
{% set _owns_msix = _msix and _msix.bar_index == k %}

{% set _slot_inner = dict(wr_valid='msix_inner_wr_valid', rd_valid='msix_inner_rd_req_valid',
                         rsp=['msix_inner_rd_rsp_ctx', 'msix_inner_rd_rsp_data', 'msix_inner_rd_rsp_valid']) if _owns_msix else {} %}
{{ bar_inst(_slot.module, k, 'i_bar' ~ k, param_size=_slot.size if _slot.has_model else none, **_slot_inner) }}
{% elif k == 1 and k not in _upper_slots %}
{{ bar_inst('pcileech_bar_impl_loopaddr', k, 'i_bar' ~ k) }}
{% else %}
{{ bar_inst('pcileech_bar_impl_none', k, 'i_bar' ~ k) }}
{% endif %}
{% endfor %}
{% else %}
{% if _msix and (_msix.bar_index != _served or _msix.bar_size != _bar_size) %}
{% error "MSI-X layout BAR" ~ _msix.bar_index ~ " does not match the served BAR" ~ _served %}
{% endif %}
{% set _inner = dict(wr_valid='msix_inner_wr_valid', rd_valid='msix_inner_rd_req_valid',
                     rsp=['msix_inner_rd_rsp_ctx', 'msix_inner_rd_rsp_data', 'msix_inner_rd_rsp_valid']) if _msix else {} %}
{% for k in range(7) %}
{% if k == _served %}
{% if _msix %}
{{ msix_subsystem(_msix, k) }}
{% endif %}
{% if _has_model %}
{{ bar_inst('pcileech_bar_impl_device', k, 'i_bar' ~ k, param_size=_bar_size, **_inner) }}
{% else %}

{% endif %}
{% elif _served64 and k == _served + 1 %}
{{ bar_inst('pcileech_bar_impl_none', k, 'i_bar' ~ k) }}
{% elif k == 1 %}
{{ bar_inst('pcileech_bar_impl_loopaddr', k, 'i_bar' ~ k) }}
{% elif k == 6 %}
{{ bar_inst('pcileech_bar_impl_none', k, 'i_bar6_optrom') }}
{% else %}
{{ bar_inst('pcileech_bar_impl_none', k, 'i_bar' ~ k) }}
{% endif %}
{% endfor %}
{% endif %}


endmodule

// NOTE: The read/write engine implementations and BAR implementation modules
// (pcileech_bar_impl_*) are not included in this template.
// They should be sourced from the upstream pcileech-fpga repository or
// generated as separate modules (e.g., pcileech_bar_impl_device.sv).

`src/templates/sv/tlp_latency_emulator.sv.j2`:

```j2
{{ header }}
//
// TLP Latency Emulator Module
// Injects realistic response latency based on captured device behavior
//
// This module delays TLP responses to emulate real device timing characteristics.
// Latency values are derived from behavior profiling of the target device.
//
// Anti-fingerprinting features:
// - Device-specific seed derived from vendor/device IDs
// - 32-bit xorshift128+ PRNG (non-trivial to reverse)
// - Burst correlation (sequential accesses have correlated timing)
// - Thermal drift simulation (gradual baseline shift over time)
// - Address-based variation (different regions have different latencies)
//

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

module tlp_latency_emulator #(
    // Timing parameters - MUST be provided from device profiling, no fallbacks
    // Using hardcoded defaults would create fingerprintable patterns
    {%- if not timing_config or timing_config.min_latency_cycles is not defined %}
    {% error "timing_config.min_latency_cycles must be provided from device profiling - no fallback allowed" %}
    {%- endif %}
    {%- if not timing_config or timing_config.max_latency_cycles is not defined %}
    {% error "timing_config.max_latency_cycles must be provided from device profiling - no fallback allowed" %}
    {%- endif %}
    {%- if not timing_config or timing_config.avg_latency_cycles is not defined %}
    {% error "timing_config.avg_latency_cycles must be provided from device profiling - no fallback allowed" %}
    {%- endif %}
    parameter MIN_LATENCY_CYCLES = {{ timing_config.min_latency_cycles }},
    parameter MAX_LATENCY_CYCLES = {{ timing_config.max_latency_cycles }},
    parameter AVG_LATENCY_CYCLES = {{ timing_config.avg_latency_cycles }},
    parameter ENABLE_JITTER = 1,
    // Device-specific seed derived from vendor_id XOR device_id XOR build entropy
    // This ensures each build has unique timing characteristics
    // SECURITY: These values MUST come from actual hardware - no fallbacks allowed
    {%- if vendor_id_int is not defined %}
    {% error "vendor_id_int must be provided from hardware - no fallback allowed to prevent fingerprinting" %}
    {%- endif %}
    {%- if device_id_int is not defined %}
    {% error "device_id_int must be provided from hardware - no fallback allowed to prevent fingerprinting" %}
    {%- endif %}
    {%- set vid = vendor_id_int %}
    {%- set did = device_id_int %}
    {%- set ssid = subsystem_id_int | default(0x0000) %}
    // Build entropy from timestamp/random source (provided by context builder)
    {%- set build_entropy = build_entropy_seed | default(range(1, 2147483647) | random) %}
    // PRNG seeds use device-specific values mixed with build entropy
    // No well-known magic constants - each combination is unique
    parameter [31:0] PRNG_SEED_0 = 32'h{{ "%08X" % ((vid | bitxor(did)) | bitxor(build_entropy)) }},
    parameter [31:0] PRNG_SEED_1 = 32'h{{ "%08X" % (((vid * 65536) | bitor(did)) | bitxor((build_entropy * 31) % 0xFFFFFFFF)) }},
    parameter [31:0] PRNG_SEED_2 = 32'h{{ "%08X" % ((did | bitxor(ssid)) | bitxor((build_entropy * 127) % 0xFFFFFFFF)) }},
    parameter [31:0] PRNG_SEED_3 = 32'h{{ "%08X" % (vid | bitxor((build_entropy * 8191) % 0xFFFFFFFF)) }},
    // Burst correlation factor (0-255, higher = more correlated sequential timing)
    // Derived from device ID to avoid fingerprinting with fixed default
    parameter BURST_CORRELATION = {{ timing_config.burst_correlation | default(128 + (vid % 128)) }},
    // Thermal drift rate (cycles between baseline adjustments)
    // Device-specific to avoid fingerprinting
    parameter THERMAL_DRIFT_PERIOD = {{ timing_config.thermal_drift_period | default(32768 + (did % 65536)) }}
)(
    input wire          clk,
    input wire          rst,
    
    // Request interface
    input wire          req_valid,
    input wire [87:0]   req_ctx,
    input wire [31:0]   req_data,
    input wire [31:0]   req_addr,    // Address for region-based latency variation
    output reg          req_ready,
    
    // Response interface (delayed)
    output reg          rsp_valid,
    output reg [87:0]   rsp_ctx,
    output reg [31:0]   rsp_data,
    input wire          rsp_ready
);

    // Latency counter and state
    reg [7:0] latency_counter;
    reg [7:0] target_latency;
    reg request_pending;
    
    // Store request data during latency period
    reg [87:0] stored_ctx;
    reg [31:0] stored_data;
    
    // Previous request tracking for burst correlation
    reg [31:0] prev_addr;
    reg [7:0]  prev_latency;
    reg        prev_valid;
    
    // ==========================================================================
    // xorshift128+ PRNG - Much harder to reverse than simple LFSR
    // State space: 2^128, passes BigCrush statistical tests
    // ==========================================================================
    reg [31:0] prng_s0, prng_s1, prng_s2, prng_s3;
    wire [31:0] prng_out;
    wire [31:0] prng_next_s0, prng_next_s3;
    
    // xorshift128+ algorithm (simplified for hardware)
    assign prng_next_s0 = prng_s0 ^ (prng_s0 << 11);
    assign prng_next_s3 = prng_s3 ^ (prng_s3 >> 19) ^ prng_next_s0 ^ (prng_next_s0 >> 8);
    assign prng_out = prng_s3 + prng_s0;  // Output is sum of states
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            // Initialize with device-specific seeds
            prng_s0 <= PRNG_SEED_0;
            prng_s1 <= PRNG_SEED_1;
            prng_s2 <= PRNG_SEED_2;
            prng_s3 <= PRNG_SEED_3;
        end else if (req_valid && req_ready) begin
            // Advance PRNG state on new request
            prng_s0 <= prng_s1;
            prng_s1 <= prng_s2;
            prng_s2 <= prng_s3;
            prng_s3 <= prng_next_s3;
        end
    end
    
    // ==========================================================================
    // Thermal drift simulation
    // Real devices show gradual timing changes due to temperature variations
    // ==========================================================================
    reg [15:0] thermal_counter;
    reg [3:0]  thermal_offset;  // -8 to +7 cycles baseline shift
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            thermal_counter <= 16'h0;
            thermal_offset <= 4'h0;
        end else begin
            thermal_counter <= thermal_counter + 1'b1;
            if (thermal_counter == THERMAL_DRIFT_PERIOD[15:0]) begin
                thermal_counter <= 16'h0;
                // Slowly drift based on PRNG low bits
                if (prng_out[0])
                    thermal_offset <= (thermal_offset < 4'h7) ? thermal_offset + 1'b1 : thermal_offset;
                else
                    thermal_offset <= (thermal_offset > 4'h8) ? thermal_offset - 1'b1 : thermal_offset;
            end
        end
    end
    
    // ==========================================================================
    // Address-based latency variation
    // Different memory regions have different access latencies (realistic)
    // ==========================================================================
    wire [2:0] addr_region;
    wire [7:0] region_latency_adjust;
    
    assign addr_region = req_addr[14:12];  // 8 regions based on address bits
    
    // Region-based latency adjustment (config space vs BAR vs extended)
    assign region_latency_adjust = (addr_region == 3'h0) ? 8'h00 :  // Config space: base latency
                                   (addr_region == 3'h1) ? 8'h02 :  // BAR0: +2 cycles
                                   (addr_region == 3'h2) ? 8'h04 :  // BAR1: +4 cycles
                                   (addr_region == 3'h3) ? 8'h01 :  // Extended config: +1 cycle
                                   8'h03;                           // Other: +3 cycles
    
    // ==========================================================================
    // Burst correlation
    // Sequential accesses to nearby addresses should have correlated timing
    // ==========================================================================
    wire is_sequential;
    wire [7:0] correlation_weight;
    wire [7:0] correlated_latency;
    
    // Detect if this access is sequential (within 256 bytes of previous)
    assign is_sequential = prev_valid && ((req_addr[31:8] == prev_addr[31:8]) ||
                                          (req_addr[31:8] == prev_addr[31:8] + 1'b1));
    
    // Weight for correlation (256 = fully correlated, 0 = independent)
    assign correlation_weight = is_sequential ? BURST_CORRELATION[7:0] : 8'h00;
    
    // Blend previous latency with new random latency based on correlation
    assign correlated_latency = ((prev_latency * correlation_weight) + 
                                 (prng_out[7:0] * (8'hFF - correlation_weight))) >> 8;
    
    // ==========================================================================
    // Final latency calculation
    // ==========================================================================
    wire [7:0] base_jitter;
    wire [7:0] jittered_latency;
    wire [7:0] thermal_adjusted;
    wire [7:0] region_adjusted;
    wire [7:0] computed_latency;
    wire [7:0] latency_range;
    
    assign latency_range = MAX_LATENCY_CYCLES - MIN_LATENCY_CYCLES + 1;
    
    // Base jitter from PRNG, modulated by correlation
    assign base_jitter = is_sequential ? correlated_latency : (prng_out[7:0] % latency_range);
    
    // Apply thermal drift
    assign thermal_adjusted = base_jitter + {% raw %}{{4{thermal_offset[3]}}, thermal_offset}{% endraw %};
    
    // Apply region-based adjustment
    assign region_adjusted = thermal_adjusted + region_latency_adjust;
    
    // Clamp to valid range
    assign jittered_latency = (MIN_LATENCY_CYCLES + region_adjusted > MAX_LATENCY_CYCLES) ?
                              MAX_LATENCY_CYCLES :
                              (MIN_LATENCY_CYCLES + region_adjusted < MIN_LATENCY_CYCLES) ?
                              MIN_LATENCY_CYCLES :
                              MIN_LATENCY_CYCLES + region_adjusted;
    
    assign computed_latency = ENABLE_JITTER ? jittered_latency : AVG_LATENCY_CYCLES;

    // Request acceptance logic
    always @(*) begin
        req_ready = !request_pending;
    end
    
    // ==========================================================================
    // Latency state machine
    // ==========================================================================
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (rst) begin
            request_pending <= 1'b0;
            latency_counter <= 8'h0;
            target_latency <= AVG_LATENCY_CYCLES;
            rsp_valid <= 1'b0;
            stored_ctx <= 88'h0;
            stored_data <= 32'h0;
            prev_addr <= 32'h0;
            prev_latency <= AVG_LATENCY_CYCLES;
            prev_valid <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            // Default: clear response valid when accepted
            if (rsp_valid && rsp_ready) begin
                rsp_valid <= 1'b0;
            end
            
            if (request_pending) begin
                // Count up latency
                if (latency_counter < target_latency) begin
                    latency_counter <= latency_counter + 8'h1;
                end else begin
                    // Latency period complete - send response
                    if (!rsp_valid || rsp_ready) begin
                        rsp_valid <= 1'b1;
                        rsp_ctx <= stored_ctx;
                        rsp_data <= stored_data;
                        request_pending <= 1'b0;
                        latency_counter <= 8'h0;
                        // Store for burst correlation
                        prev_latency <= target_latency;
                        prev_valid <= 1'b1;
                    end
                end
            end else if (req_valid && req_ready) begin
                // New request - store and start latency counter
                request_pending <= 1'b1;
                stored_ctx <= req_ctx;
                stored_data <= req_data;
                prev_addr <= req_addr;
                latency_counter <= 8'h0;
                target_latency <= computed_latency;
            end
        end
    end

endmodule

`src/templates/sv/vendor/verilog-pcie/README.md`:

```md
# Vendored: verilog-pcie `pcie_msix.v`

MSI-X table/PBA storage and interrupt message generation, used by the MSI-X
subsystem summarized in `docs/development/MSIX_STATUS.md`.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Upstream | <https://github.com/alexforencich/verilog-pcie> |
| Revision | `25156a9a162c41c60f11f41590c7d006d015ae5a` |
| File | `rtl/pcie_msix.v` |
| Upstream SHA-256 | `85da9abfe32cc3ca92934ac9ae2c1228da606496e8762a9015766791410d9570` |
| License | MIT, see `LICENSE` (upstream `COPYING`); file header retained |

`tests/test_vendored_pcie_msix.py` checks that the vendored file equals the
upstream file plus exactly the modifications below. The MX-04 and MX-05 hunks
live in `tests/pcie_msix_local_patches.py`, generated layer by layer. Update
them together with the core.

## Local modifications

1. **Provenance comment** after the upstream license header.
2. **MX-02 PBA write address.** Upstream sets the default
   `pba_mem_addr = irq_index_reg >> 5`. The pending-bit set path
   (`STATE_READ_TBL_2`) and clear path (`STATE_SEND_TLP`) both rely on that
   default, but every PBA read uses `>> 6` on 64-bit PBA words. As a result,
   vectors whose index mod 64 is 32 or higher lose their pending bit or corrupt
   another vector's pending word. The fix changes the default to `>> 6`.
   Regression coverage is in `tests/test_vendored_pcie_msix.py`.

```diff
-    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_reg >> 5;
+    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_reg >> 6; // MX-02: PBA words are 64 bits; upstream used >> 5
```

3. **MX-02b stale PBA word.** The pending-bit scan trusts `pba_mem_rd_data_reg`,
   but every PBA write blocks that cycle's read. After `STATE_SEND_TLP` clears
   vector 63 and advances to vector 64, the scan reads vector 0's pending bit
   as vector 64's. The same happens at the wrap from the top index back to 0.
   - Observed: when vector 64 had never been programmed, the core wrote to
     host address 0.
   - Fix: a new `pba_word_valid_reg`, cleared by any PBA write and set by any
     PBA read. The scan refreshes the word before testing a bit.
4. **MX-02b head-of-line livelock.** A pending vector that is still masked
   re-entered `READ_TBL_1`/`READ_TBL_2` without advancing the index, so the
   scan never reached other pending vectors once they were unmasked.
   - Fix: the masked branch of `STATE_READ_TBL_2` now advances `irq_index_next`.
5. **MX-02b Mask default.** `tbl_mem` started at all zeros, so every Vector
   Control Mask bit was 0. Raising a vector the host had never programmed sent
   a write of 0 to address 0. The PCIe Base Specification gives the MSI-X
   Vector Control Mask bit a default of 1b.
   - Fix: odd table words (Vector Control and Message Data) now initialize to
     `64'h0000000100000000`.

6. **MX-04 host port.** The upstream AXI-lite slave accepts at most one access
   every two clocks, and its table RAM serves a host read or a host write per
   clock, not both. The PCILeech BAR engines issue up to one read and one write
   per clock and cannot be stalled.
   - Replaced by `host_wr_*`/`host_rd_*`: DWORD-indexed, no handshake, read
     data exactly two clocks after the request (the latency of the other
     served-BAR implementations).
   - The table is duplicated. Each host write updates `tbl_mem` (read by the
     scan) and `tbl_host_mem` (read by the host) in the same clock.
   - A host read of the word written in the same clock returns the new bytes.
   - PBA host writes are ignored; host reads use a second PBA read port.
   - `AXIL_*` parameters and ports are gone. The MX-02 Icarus regressions run
     on this port; the pristine-upstream test still uses AXI-lite.
   - Synthesis on `xc7a100tfgg484-1` (Vivado 2026.1, out of context, with the
     router, routed at 125 MHz): 2048 vectors use 16 BRAM tiles, 421 LUTs,
     WNS +0.59 ns; 6 vectors use 2 BRAM tiles, 211 LUTs, WNS +2.60 ns.

7. **MX-05 live controls and reset.** New ports `bus_master_enable`,
   `msix_clear` and `msix_clearing`; state widened to 3 bits with
   `STATE_WAIT_TLP` and `STATE_CLEAR`. The contracts are below.

### MX-05 contracts

The integration (MX-07) drives `msix_enable`/`msix_mask` from the hard IP's
`cfg_interrupt_msixenable`/`cfg_interrupt_msixfm`, `bus_master_enable` from
`cfg_command[2]`, and `msix_clear` from the PCIe-defined resets: the IP's user
reset (PERST and link down), hot reset and FLR.

- **Reset.** `msix_clear` aborts any operation, withdraws a presented message,
  and starts a sweep (`msix_clearing` high) that writes every table entry to
  its reset value (address and data 0, Mask 1) and every PBA word to 0. The
  sweep takes `2**(IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH+1)` clocks, at most 4096 (66 us at
  62.5 MHz), well inside the 100 ms the host must wait after a reset or FLR.
  Requests wait (`irq_ready` low) and host table writes are dropped while it
  runs. A clear requested during `rst` completes after `rst`.
- **`rst` preserves state.** `rst` includes PCILeech's own soft reset, which is
  not a PCIe reset, so it resets control state and withdraws a presented
  message but keeps the table and PBA. A withdrawn scan-path message stays
  pending; a withdrawn direct request is dropped.
- **Sending.** A message is sent only while MSI-X is enabled, the function is
  unmasked, Bus Master Enable is set, and the vector is unmasked, read from the
  table in the two clocks before it is presented.
- **Presented messages.** Once presented (`tx_wr_req_tlp_valid`), a message is
  owned by the core until accepted or withdrawn; the FSM handles nothing else
  meanwhile. If the controls dropped between the table read and presentation,
  it is never presented. It is withdrawn before acceptance if the function is
  masked or bus mastering is turned off (it becomes pending again), or if MSI-X
  is disabled: a direct request is then dropped, and a vector found by the scan
  keeps the pending bit it already had. A per-vector mask set after
  presentation does not withdraw it, because the core does not re-read the
  table. MX-06 bounds that window (see below).
- **Requests while disabled.** A request while MSI-X Enable is clear is
  dropped, not recorded, so a driver enabling MSI-X later does not receive
  events from before. Pending bits already set are kept.
- **Fairness.** A request does not move the scan. After each accepted request,
  the scan gets the next two idle steps (the first may only refresh the PBA
  word), so a producer holding `irq_valid` high cannot starve pending vectors.
  The request rate drops by at most two clocks per request.

Each MX-02 fix has a regression, plus a test that reverts that fix alone and
checks the regression then fails (`test_each_fix_is_detected_when_reverted`).
Host-port behavior is covered by `tests/test_msix_bar_router.py`.

## Integration notes

No producer drives `irq_valid`, so the generated controller ties it low and
never sends a message.

The integration (MX-07) is generated by
`src/templates/sv/msix/_msix_subsystem.j2`, called from the BAR controller
template when the build's MSI-X decision (`device_clone/msix_subsystem.py`)
generates the subsystem. The live controls and the IP user reset reach the
controller through voltcyclone-fpga's read-only `IfPCIeSignals.mpro` port
(`pcie_ctx`, `rst_pcie_user`, upstream PR #6). The points below say how each
contract is wired.

- **Transmit (MX-06).** `src/templates/sv/msix/pcileech_msix_tlp_tx.sv`
  commits the presented message into a one-message buffer whenever the buffer
  is empty, so the core's wait in `STATE_WAIT_TLP` lasts at most until the
  previous message leaves. The window in which a per-vector mask, function
  mask or Bus Master Enable change cannot stop a message is therefore the
  presentation clock plus the time a committed message waits for the stream:
  at most the completion packet already in progress or selected, then the
  upstream mux and link. A committed message cannot be withdrawn, because the
  upstream mux locks onto an input once it reports `has_data`.
- **Clear drain.** The controller feeds the PCIe resets (`rst_pcie_user`,
  `pl_received_hot_rst`, `cfg_received_func_lvl_rst`) into the merger's
  `clear_req` and drives the core's `msix_clear` from the merger's
  `clear_out`. That holds the clear until a message committed before it has
  left, so it always goes out before the driver can program a new entry.
- **`msg_allow`.** The controller drives the merger's `msg_allow` from the live
  `cfg_interrupt_msixenable && !cfg_interrupt_msixfm && cfg_command[2] &&
  !clear_req`. The core registers those one clock late, and the gate on
  `msg_ready` stops a commit in that clock. Gating on `clear_req` rather than
  the core's `msix_clear` (`clear_out`) is equivalent: the two differ only
  while a committed message is buffered, and `msg_ready` is low then anyway.
- **`requester_id`.** PCILeech's `pcie_id` is `{function[2:0], device[4:0],
  bus[7:0]}`, not PCIe order. The controller feeds
  `{pcie_id[7:0], pcie_id[12:8], pcie_id[15:13]}`. Keep
  `TLP_FORCE_64_BIT_ADDR=0`: a 4DW header for an address below 4 GiB is
  malformed.

- **Reserved bits.** Vector Control bits [31:1] are stored and read back as
  written. Pinned by
  `test_known_behavior_vector_control_reserved_bits_are_stored`. Left as is
  on purpose: with TPH, Vector Control bits [31:16] can hold steering tags, so
  forcing them to 0 would be wrong for such donors.
- **Unconfirmed upstream behaviors.** These came out of review and are
  not reproduced:
  - A host table write landing between `READ_TBL_1` and `READ_TBL_2` can tear
    an entry. The spec forbids changing an unmasked entry.
  - While `rst` is held, the FSM is forced idle each clock, so at most one PBA
    write from the state before `rst` lands. (Analysis, not a reproduction.)
- **Layout.** Donor table/PBA offsets are translated by
  `src/templates/sv/msix/pcileech_msix_bar_router.sv`. `requester_id` must come
  from the live bus/device/function (`pcie_id`).
- **Same-clock scan read.** A host write landing in the clock the scan reads
  the same table word returns the old word to the scan. The spec forbids
  changing an unmasked entry, so this matters only together with the torn-entry
  hypothesis above.

```

`src/templates/sv/vendor/verilog-pcie/pcie_msix.v`:

```v

// Vendored from https://github.com/alexforencich/verilog-pcie
// revision 25156a9a162c41c60f11f41590c7d006d015ae5a, rtl/pcie_msix.v.
// Local modifications (see README.md in this directory):
//   MX-02: default PBA write address uses >> 6 (64-bit PBA words), was >> 5.
//   MX-02b: scan re-reads the PBA word after any PBA write (stale-word fix);
//           masked branch advances the scan index (head-of-line fix);
//           Vector Control Mask bits reset to 1 (PCIe default).
//   MX-04: a single-clock host port and a duplicated table replace the
//          AXI-lite slave (one host read and one host write every clock).
//   MX-05: msix_clear sweep, Bus Master Enable gating, a commit/withdraw
//          contract for presented messages, requests dropped while disabled,
//          and scan fairness under continuous requests.

// Language: Verilog 2001

`resetall
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none

/*
 * PCIe MSI-X module
 */
module pcie_msix #
(
    // Interrupt configuration
    parameter IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH = 11,

    // TLP interface configuration
    parameter TLP_HDR_WIDTH = 128,
    parameter TLP_FORCE_64_BIT_ADDR = 0
)
(
    input  wire                        clk,
    input  wire                        rst,

    /*
     * MX-04: host access port for the MSI-X table and PBA (replaces the
     * upstream AXI-lite slave). Accepts one read and one write every clock,
     * with no backpressure. Addresses are DWORD indices within the table
     * (pba=0) or the PBA (pba=1); PBA writes are ignored. host_rd_data is
     * valid exactly two clocks after host_rd_valid.
     */
    input  wire                        host_wr_valid,
    input  wire                        host_wr_pba,
    input  wire [IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH+1:0]  host_wr_dw,
    input  wire [31:0]                 host_wr_data,
    input  wire [3:0]                  host_wr_be,
    input  wire                        host_rd_valid,
    input  wire                        host_rd_pba,
    input  wire [IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH+1:0]  host_rd_dw,
    output wire [31:0]                 host_rd_data,

    /*
     * Interrupt request input
     */
    input  wire [IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH-1:0]  irq_index,
    input  wire                        irq_valid,
    output wire                        irq_ready,

    /*
     * Memory write TLP output
     */
    output wire [31:0]                 tx_wr_req_tlp_data,
    output wire                        tx_wr_req_tlp_strb,
    output wire [TLP_HDR_WIDTH-1:0]    tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr,
    output wire                        tx_wr_req_tlp_valid,
    output wire                        tx_wr_req_tlp_sop,
    output wire                        tx_wr_req_tlp_eop,
    input  wire                        tx_wr_req_tlp_ready,

    /*
     * Configuration
     */
    input  wire [15:0]                 requester_id,
    input  wire                        msix_enable,
    input  wire                        msix_mask,

    /*
     * MX-05: live controls and reset (contracts in README.md)
     */
    input  wire                        bus_master_enable,
    input  wire                        msix_clear,
    output wire                        msix_clearing
);

parameter TBL_ADDR_WIDTH = IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH+1;
parameter PBA_ADDR_WIDTH = IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH > 6 ? IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH-6 : 0;
parameter PBA_ADDR_WIDTH_INT = PBA_ADDR_WIDTH > 0 ? PBA_ADDR_WIDTH : 1;

// bus width assertions
initial begin
    if (IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH > 11) begin
        $error("Error: IRQ index width must be 11 or less (instance %m)");
        $finish;
    end
end

localparam [2:0]
    TLP_FMT_3DW = 3'b000,
    TLP_FMT_4DW = 3'b001,
    TLP_FMT_3DW_DATA = 3'b010,
    TLP_FMT_4DW_DATA = 3'b011,
    TLP_FMT_PREFIX = 3'b100;

localparam [2:0]
    STATE_IDLE = 3'd0,
    STATE_READ_TBL_1 = 3'd1,
    STATE_READ_TBL_2 = 3'd2,
    STATE_SEND_TLP = 3'd3,
    STATE_WAIT_TLP = 3'd4, // MX-05: message presented, awaiting acceptance or withdrawal
    STATE_CLEAR = 3'd5;    // MX-05: table and PBA reset sweep

reg [2:0] state_reg = STATE_IDLE, state_next;

reg [IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH-1:0] irq_index_reg = 0, irq_index_next;

reg [63:0] vec_addr_reg = 0, vec_addr_next;
reg [31:0] vec_data_reg = 0, vec_data_next;
reg vec_mask_reg = 1'b0, vec_mask_next;

reg [127:0] tlp_hdr;

reg tbl_mem_rd_en;
reg [TBL_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] tbl_mem_addr;
reg pba_mem_rd_en;
reg pba_mem_wr_en;
reg [PBA_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] pba_mem_addr;
reg [63:0] pba_mem_wr_data;

reg irq_ready_reg = 1'b0, irq_ready_next;

reg [31:0] tx_wr_req_tlp_data_reg = 0, tx_wr_req_tlp_data_next;
reg [TLP_HDR_WIDTH-1:0] tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr_reg = 0, tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr_next;
reg tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_reg = 0, tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_next;

reg msix_enable_reg = 1'b0;
reg msix_mask_reg = 1'b0;
reg bus_master_enable_reg = 1'b0;
// MX-05: messages may be sent only with MSI-X enabled, unmasked and bus mastering
wire scan_allowed = msix_enable_reg && !msix_mask_reg && bus_master_enable_reg;
// MX-05: clear sweep index over table words; PBA words use its low bits
reg [TBL_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] clear_index_reg = 0, clear_index_next;
// MX-05: after a request is accepted, the next idle step belongs to the PBA scan
reg scan_owed_reg = 1'b0, scan_owed_next;
// MX-05: a request does not move the scan; it resumes from scan_resume_reg
reg [IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH-1:0] scan_resume_reg = 0, scan_resume_next;
reg from_request_reg = 1'b0, from_request_next;
reg scan_turn;
// MX-05: the scan has taken one step of its turn (the first may only refresh
// the PBA word, so at most two steps are owed)
reg scan_stepped_reg = 1'b0, scan_stepped_next;

// MSI-X table
(* ramstyle = "no_rw_check, mlab" *)
reg [63:0] tbl_mem[(2**TBL_ADDR_WIDTH)-1:0];
// MX-04: host-read copy of the table. Every host write updates both copies in
// the same clock; the scan reads tbl_mem and the host reads tbl_host_mem, so
// neither memory needs more than one write and one read port.
reg [63:0] tbl_host_mem[(2**TBL_ADDR_WIDTH)-1:0];

// MSI-X PBA
(* ram_style = "distributed", ramstyle = "no_rw_check, mlab" *)
reg [63:0] pba_mem[(2**PBA_ADDR_WIDTH)-1:0];

reg [63:0] tbl_mem_rd_data_reg = 0;
reg [63:0] pba_mem_rd_data_reg = 0;
// MX-02b: pba_mem_rd_data_reg holds the PBA word for irq_index_reg's group
reg pba_word_valid_reg = 1'b0, pba_word_valid_next;

// MX-04 host port: the table word is (DWORD index >> 1); bit 0 picks the half.
wire [TBL_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] host_wr_index = host_wr_dw >> 1;
wire [TBL_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] host_rd_index = host_rd_dw >> 1;
wire host_tbl_wr = host_wr_valid && !host_wr_pba && state_reg != STATE_CLEAR;
wire [7:0] host_wr_be64 = host_wr_dw[0] ? {host_wr_be, 4'b0000} : {4'b0000, host_wr_be};
wire [63:0] host_wr_data64 = {host_wr_data, host_wr_data};
// MX-05: one byte-enabled write port shared by host writes and the reset sweep
// (host table writes are dropped while the sweep runs), so RAM inference holds
wire tbl_wr_clear = state_reg == STATE_CLEAR;
wire [TBL_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] tbl_wr_addr = tbl_wr_clear ? clear_index_reg : host_wr_index;
wire [63:0] tbl_wr_data = tbl_wr_clear ? (clear_index_reg[0] ? 64'h0000000100000000 : 64'd0) : host_wr_data64;
wire [7:0] tbl_wr_be = tbl_wr_clear ? 8'hFF : (host_tbl_wr ? host_wr_be64 : 8'h00);

reg [63:0] host_tbl_rd_reg = 0;
reg [63:0] host_pba_rd_reg = 0;
reg host_rd_pba_reg = 1'b0;
reg host_rd_hi_reg = 1'b0;
// Bytes of a same-clock table write to the word being read: the read sees them.
reg [7:0] host_bypass_be_reg = 0;
reg [63:0] host_bypass_data_reg = 0;
reg [63:0] host_rd_word;
reg [31:0] host_rd_data_reg = 0;

assign host_rd_data = host_rd_data_reg;

assign irq_ready = irq_ready_reg && !(scan_owed_reg && scan_allowed);
assign msix_clearing = state_reg == STATE_CLEAR;

assign tx_wr_req_tlp_data = tx_wr_req_tlp_data_reg;
assign tx_wr_req_tlp_strb = 1;
assign tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr = tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr_reg;
assign tx_wr_req_tlp_valid = tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_reg;
assign tx_wr_req_tlp_sop = 1'b1;
assign tx_wr_req_tlp_eop = 1'b1;

integer i;

initial begin
    for (i = 0; i < 2**TBL_ADDR_WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin
        // MX-02b: odd words hold Vector Control; its Mask bit defaults to 1
        tbl_mem[i] = (i & 1) ? 64'h0000000100000000 : 64'd0;
        tbl_host_mem[i] = (i & 1) ? 64'h0000000100000000 : 64'd0;
    end
    for (i = 0; i < 2**PBA_ADDR_WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin
        pba_mem[i] = 0;
    end
end

always @* begin
    state_next = STATE_IDLE;

    tbl_mem_rd_en = 1'b0;
    tbl_mem_addr = {irq_index_reg, 1'b0};

    pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b0;
    pba_mem_wr_en = 1'b0;
    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_reg >> 6; // MX-02: PBA words are 64 bits; upstream used >> 5
    pba_mem_wr_data = 0;

    irq_index_next = irq_index_reg;
    clear_index_next = clear_index_reg;
    scan_owed_next = scan_owed_reg;
    scan_resume_next = scan_resume_reg;
    from_request_next = from_request_reg;
    scan_turn = 1'b0;
    scan_stepped_next = scan_stepped_reg;

    vec_addr_next = vec_addr_reg;
    vec_data_next = vec_data_reg;
    vec_mask_next = vec_mask_reg;

    irq_ready_next = 1'b0;

    tx_wr_req_tlp_data_next = tx_wr_req_tlp_data_reg;
    tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr_next = tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr_reg;
    tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_next = tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_reg && !tx_wr_req_tlp_ready;

    // TLP header
    // DW 0
    if (((vec_addr_reg[63:2] >> 30) != 0) || TLP_FORCE_64_BIT_ADDR) begin
        tlp_hdr[127:125] = TLP_FMT_4DW_DATA; // fmt - 4DW with data
    end else begin
        tlp_hdr[127:125] = TLP_FMT_3DW_DATA; // fmt - 3DW with data
    end
    tlp_hdr[124:120] = 5'b00000; // type - write
    tlp_hdr[119] = 1'b0; // T9
    tlp_hdr[118:116] = 3'b000; // TC
    tlp_hdr[115] = 1'b0; // T8
    tlp_hdr[114] = 1'b0; // attr
    tlp_hdr[113] = 1'b0; // LN
    tlp_hdr[112] = 1'b0; // TH
    tlp_hdr[111] = 1'b0; // TD
    tlp_hdr[110] = 1'b0; // EP
    tlp_hdr[109:108] = 2'b00; // attr
    tlp_hdr[107:106] = 3'b000; // AT
    tlp_hdr[105:96] = 10'd1; // length
    // DW 1
    tlp_hdr[95:80] = requester_id; // requester ID
    tlp_hdr[79:72] = 8'd0; // tag
    tlp_hdr[71:68] = 4'b0000; // last BE
    tlp_hdr[67:64] = 4'b1111; // first BE
    if (((vec_addr_reg[63:2] >> 30) != 0) || TLP_FORCE_64_BIT_ADDR) begin
        // DW 2+3
        tlp_hdr[63:2] = vec_addr_reg[63:2]; // address
        tlp_hdr[1:0] = 2'b00; // PH
    end else begin
        // DW 2
        tlp_hdr[63:34] = vec_addr_reg[63:2]; // address
        tlp_hdr[33:32] = 2'b00; // PH
        // DW 3
        tlp_hdr[31:0] = 32'd0;
    end

    case (state_reg)
        STATE_IDLE: begin
            irq_ready_next = 1'b1;

            if (irq_valid && irq_ready) begin
                // new request
                irq_ready_next = 1'b0;
                irq_index_next = irq_index;
                // MX-05: remember the scan position; the scan gets the next step
                scan_owed_next = 1'b1;
                scan_resume_next = irq_index_reg;
                from_request_next = 1'b1;

                tbl_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                tbl_mem_addr = {irq_index_next, 1'b0};

                pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                pba_mem_addr = irq_index_next >> 6;

                state_next = STATE_READ_TBL_1;
            end else if ((!irq_valid || scan_owed_reg) && scan_allowed) begin
                // MX-05: a waiting request yields one step to the scan, so
                // continuous requests cannot starve pending vectors
                scan_turn = 1'b1;
                from_request_next = 1'b0;
                // no new request waiting, scan PBA for masked requests

                if (!pba_word_valid_reg) begin
                    // MX-02b: cached word was invalidated by a PBA write; refresh it
                    pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_reg >> 6;

                    state_next = STATE_IDLE;
                end else if (pba_mem_rd_data_reg[irq_index_reg & 6'h3f]) begin
                    // PBA bit for current index is set, try issuing it
                    irq_ready_next = 1'b0;

                    tbl_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                    tbl_mem_addr = {irq_index_next, 1'b0};

                    pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_next >> 6;

                    state_next = STATE_READ_TBL_1;
                end else begin
                    // PBA bit for current index is not set
                    if (pba_mem_rd_data_reg) begin
                        // at least one bit set in current group, move to next index
                        irq_index_next = irq_index_reg + 1;
                    end else begin
                        // no bits set in current group, move to next group
                        irq_index_next = (irq_index_reg & ({IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH{1'b1}} << 6)) + 7'd64;
                    end

                    pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_next >> 6;

                    state_next = STATE_IDLE;
                end
            end else begin
                state_next = STATE_IDLE;
            end
        end
        STATE_READ_TBL_1: begin
            // handle first table read
            tbl_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
            tbl_mem_addr = {irq_index_reg, 1'b1};

            vec_addr_next = {tbl_mem_rd_data_reg[63:2], 2'b00};

            state_next = STATE_READ_TBL_2;
        end
        STATE_READ_TBL_2: begin
            // handle second table read
            vec_data_next = tbl_mem_rd_data_reg[31:0];
            vec_mask_next = tbl_mem_rd_data_reg[32];

            if (scan_allowed && !vec_mask_next) begin
                // send TLP
                state_next = STATE_SEND_TLP;
            end else if (!msix_enable_reg) begin
                // MX-05: a request while MSI-X is disabled is dropped, not recorded
                if (from_request_reg) begin
                    // MX-05: resume the scan where the request interrupted it
                    irq_index_next = scan_resume_reg;
                    if (!pba_mem_wr_en) begin
                        pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                        pba_mem_addr = scan_resume_reg >> 6;
                    end
                end
                irq_ready_next = 1'b1;
                state_next = STATE_IDLE;
            end else begin
                // set PBA bit
                pba_mem_wr_en = 1'b1;
                pba_mem_wr_data = pba_mem_rd_data_reg | (1 << (irq_index_reg & 6'h3F));
                // MX-02b: move past a still-masked vector so the scan cannot livelock on it
                irq_index_next = irq_index_reg + 1;
                if (from_request_reg) begin
                    // MX-05: resume the scan where the request interrupted it
                    irq_index_next = scan_resume_reg;
                    if (!pba_mem_wr_en) begin
                        pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                        pba_mem_addr = scan_resume_reg >> 6;
                    end
                end
                irq_ready_next = 1'b1;
                state_next = STATE_IDLE;
            end
        end
        STATE_SEND_TLP: begin
            // MX-05: present the message, then wait until it is accepted or
            // withdrawn; the FSM owns it until then, so it cannot be lost.
            // If the controls dropped since READ_TBL_2, WAIT_TLP withdraws it
            // without presenting.
            tx_wr_req_tlp_data_next = vec_data_reg;
            tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr_next = tlp_hdr;
            tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_next = scan_allowed;
            state_next = STATE_WAIT_TLP;
        end
        STATE_WAIT_TLP: begin
            if (tx_wr_req_tlp_valid && tx_wr_req_tlp_ready) begin
                // accepted: delivered, clear the PBA bit
                pba_mem_wr_en = 1'b1;
                pba_mem_wr_data = pba_mem_rd_data_reg & ~(1 << (irq_index_reg & 6'h3F));

                // increment index so we don't check the same PBA bit immediately
                irq_index_next = irq_index_reg + 1;
                if (from_request_reg) begin
                    // MX-05: resume the scan where the request interrupted it
                    irq_index_next = scan_resume_reg;
                    if (!pba_mem_wr_en) begin
                        pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                        pba_mem_addr = scan_resume_reg >> 6;
                    end
                end

                irq_ready_next = 1'b1;
                state_next = STATE_IDLE;
            end else if (!scan_allowed || !tx_wr_req_tlp_valid) begin
                // withdrawn before acceptance (or never presented): re-pend while MSI-X stays
                // enabled (function mask or bus mastering off). If MSI-X is
                // disabled, a direct request is dropped and a scanned vector
                // keeps the pending bit it already had (PBA unchanged).
                tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_next = 1'b0;
                if (msix_enable_reg) begin
                    pba_mem_wr_en = 1'b1;
                    pba_mem_wr_data = pba_mem_rd_data_reg | (1 << (irq_index_reg & 6'h3F));
                end else if (from_request_reg) begin
                    pba_mem_wr_en = 1'b1;
                    pba_mem_wr_data = pba_mem_rd_data_reg & ~(1 << (irq_index_reg & 6'h3F));
                end
                irq_index_next = irq_index_reg + 1;
                if (from_request_reg) begin
                    // MX-05: resume the scan where the request interrupted it
                    irq_index_next = scan_resume_reg;
                    if (!pba_mem_wr_en) begin
                        pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;
                        pba_mem_addr = scan_resume_reg >> 6;
                    end
                end
                irq_ready_next = 1'b1;
                state_next = STATE_IDLE;
            end else begin
                state_next = STATE_WAIT_TLP;
            end
        end
        STATE_CLEAR: begin
            // reset sweep: every PBA word to 0 here, every table word to its
            // reset value (Mask=1, address/data 0) in the host write block
            pba_mem_wr_en = 1'b1;
            pba_mem_addr = clear_index_reg & ((2**PBA_ADDR_WIDTH)-1);
            pba_mem_wr_data = 0;
            clear_index_next = clear_index_reg + 1;
            if (&clear_index_reg) begin
                irq_index_next = 0;
                irq_ready_next = 1'b1;
                state_next = STATE_IDLE;
            end else begin
                state_next = STATE_CLEAR;
            end
        end
        default: begin
            state_next = STATE_IDLE;
        end
    endcase

    // MX-02b: a PBA write invalidates the cached word; a read refreshes it
    pba_word_valid_next = pba_mem_wr_en ? 1'b0 : (pba_mem_rd_en ? 1'b1 : pba_word_valid_reg);

    // MX-05: a scan turn is two scan steps: the first may only refresh the
    // PBA word, the second then tests a pending bit. Counting steps (rather
    // than looking at the next index) keeps this off the PBA scan's timing path.
    if (scan_turn) begin
        scan_stepped_next = !scan_stepped_reg;
        if (scan_stepped_reg) begin
            scan_owed_next = 1'b0;
        end
    end

    // MX-05: a clear request (link down/PERST, hot reset, FLR) aborts any
    // operation, withdraws a presented message and restarts the sweep
    if (msix_clear) begin
        state_next = STATE_CLEAR;
        clear_index_next = 0;
        tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_next = 1'b0;
        pba_mem_wr_en = 1'b0;
        irq_ready_next = 1'b0;
        scan_owed_next = 1'b0;
        scan_stepped_next = 1'b0;
        from_request_next = 1'b0;
    end
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    state_reg <= state_next;

    irq_index_reg <= irq_index_next;
    pba_word_valid_reg <= pba_word_valid_next;

    vec_addr_reg <= vec_addr_next;
    vec_data_reg <= vec_data_next;
    vec_mask_reg <= vec_mask_next;

    irq_ready_reg <= irq_ready_next;

    tx_wr_req_tlp_data_reg <= tx_wr_req_tlp_data_next;
    tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr_reg <= tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr_next;
    tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_reg <= tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_next;

    msix_enable_reg <= msix_enable;
    msix_mask_reg <= msix_mask;
    bus_master_enable_reg <= bus_master_enable;
    clear_index_reg <= clear_index_next;
    scan_owed_reg <= scan_owed_next;
    scan_stepped_reg <= scan_stepped_next;
    scan_resume_reg <= scan_resume_next;
    from_request_reg <= from_request_next;

    if (tbl_mem_rd_en) begin
        tbl_mem_rd_data_reg <= tbl_mem[tbl_mem_addr];
    end

    if (pba_mem_wr_en) begin
        pba_mem[pba_mem_addr] <= pba_mem_wr_data;
    end else if (pba_mem_rd_en) begin
        pba_mem_rd_data_reg <= pba_mem[pba_mem_addr];
    end

    if (rst) begin
        state_reg <= STATE_IDLE;
        pba_word_valid_reg <= 1'b0;

        irq_ready_reg <= 1'b0;

        tx_wr_req_tlp_valid_reg <= 1'b0;
        scan_owed_reg <= 1'b0;
        scan_stepped_reg <= 1'b0;
        from_request_reg <= 1'b0;
        // MX-05: rst (which includes PCILeech's own soft reset) does not clear
        // the table or PBA, but must not abort a clear sweep in progress
        if (state_next == STATE_CLEAR) begin
            state_reg <= STATE_CLEAR;
        end
    end
end

// MX-04 host port: fixed two-clock read latency, one read and one write per clock
always @* begin
    for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) begin
        host_rd_word[8*i +: 8] = host_bypass_be_reg[i] ? host_bypass_data_reg[8*i +: 8] : host_tbl_rd_reg[8*i +: 8];
    end
    if (host_rd_pba_reg) begin
        host_rd_word = host_pba_rd_reg;
    end
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) begin
        if (tbl_wr_be[i]) begin
            tbl_mem[tbl_wr_addr][8*i +: 8] <= tbl_wr_data[8*i +: 8];
            tbl_host_mem[tbl_wr_addr][8*i +: 8] <= tbl_wr_data[8*i +: 8];
        end
    end

    // Clock 1: read both stores and note any same-clock write to the word.
    host_tbl_rd_reg <= tbl_host_mem[host_rd_index];
    host_pba_rd_reg <= pba_mem[host_rd_dw >> 1];
    host_rd_pba_reg <= host_rd_pba;
    host_rd_hi_reg <= host_rd_dw[0];
    host_bypass_be_reg <= (host_tbl_wr && host_rd_valid && !host_rd_pba && host_wr_index == host_rd_index) ? host_wr_be64 : 8'd0;
    host_bypass_data_reg <= host_wr_data64;

    // Clock 2: select the DWORD.
    host_rd_data_reg <= host_rd_hi_reg ? host_rd_word[63:32] : host_rd_word[31:0];
end

endmodule

`resetall

`src/templates/template_mapping.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Template path mapping for the overlay-only architecture.

This module provides minimal mappings for the active templates used
in the current overlay-only architecture where only .coe configuration
files are generated.
"""

# Mapping from old paths to new paths (minimal - only active templates)
TEMPLATE_PATH_MAPPING = {
    # Active SystemVerilog template (config space overlay)
    "systemverilog/pcileech_cfgspace.coe.j2": "sv/pcileech_cfgspace.coe.j2",
    # Python templates
    "python/build_integration.py.j2": "python/build_integration.py.j2",
    "python/pcileech_build_integration.py.j2": "python/pcileech_build_integration.py.j2",
}


def get_new_template_path(old_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Get the new template path for a given old path.

    Args:
        old_path: The old nested template path

    Returns:
        The new flattened template path
    """
    # Remove leading slashes and normalize
    old_path = old_path.lstrip("/")

    # Check if we have a mapping
    if old_path in TEMPLATE_PATH_MAPPING:
        return TEMPLATE_PATH_MAPPING[old_path]

    # If no mapping exists, return the original path
    # This allows for gradual migration
    return old_path


def update_template_path(template_name: str) -> str:
    """
    Update a template name to use the new path structure.

    This function handles both old and new path formats gracefully.

    Args:
        template_name: The template name (may include path)

    Returns:
        The updated template path
    """
    # If it's already using the new structure, return as-is
    if template_name.startswith(("sv/", "tcl/", "python/")):
        return template_name

    # Otherwise, map it
    mapped = get_new_template_path(template_name)

    # Convenience fallback: if caller provided a bare .coe template
    # filename without a directory prefix, assume it lives under the "sv/" folder.
    if "/" not in mapped and mapped.endswith(".coe.j2"):
        return f"sv/{mapped}"

    return mapped

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Advanced SystemVerilog Error Handling Module

This module provides comprehensive error detection, handling, and recovery logic
for PCIe devices, including correctable/uncorrectable errors, retry mechanisms,
and error logging.

Advanced Error Handling feature for the PCILeechFWGenerator project.
"""

from typing import Optional

from .sv_config import ErrorHandlingConfig
from .template_renderer import TemplateRenderer


class ErrorHandlingGenerator:
    """Generator for advanced error handling SystemVerilog logic."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: Optional[ErrorHandlingConfig] = None,
        renderer: Optional[TemplateRenderer] = None,
    ):
        """Initialize the error handling generator.
        
        Args:
            config: Error handling configuration (uses defaults if None)
            renderer: Shared TemplateRenderer instance (creates new if None)
        """
        self.config = config or ErrorHandlingConfig()
        self.renderer = renderer if renderer is not None else TemplateRenderer()

    def generate_error_declarations(self) -> str:
        """Generate error handling signal declarations."""
        context = {"config": self.config}
        return self.renderer.render_template(
            "sv/error_handling/error_declarations.sv.j2", context
        )

    def generate_error_detection(self) -> str:
        """Generate error detection logic."""
        context = {"config": self.config}
        return self.renderer.render_template(
            "sv/error_handling/error_detection.sv.j2", context
        )

    def generate_error_state_machine(self) -> str:
        """Generate error handling state machine."""
        context = {"config": self.config}
        return self.renderer.render_template(
            "sv/error_handling/error_state_machine.sv.j2", context
        )

    def generate_error_logging(self) -> str:
        """Generate error logging logic."""
        context = {"config": self.config}
        return self.renderer.render_template(
            "sv/error_handling/error_logging.sv.j2", context
        )

    def generate_error_counters(self) -> str:
        """Generate error counting logic."""
        context = {"config": self.config}
        return self.renderer.render_template(
            "sv/error_handling/error_counters.sv.j2", context
        )

    def generate_error_outputs(self) -> str:
        """Generate error output assignments."""
        context = {"config": self.config}
        return self.renderer.render_template(
            "sv/error_handling/error_outputs.sv.j2", context
        )

    def generate_complete_error_handling(self) -> str:
        """Generate complete error handling logic."""
        context = {"config": self.config}
        return self.renderer.render_template(
            "sv/error_handling_complete.sv.j2", context
        )
