`tests/test_vendored_pcie_msix.py`:

```py
"""Provenance and Icarus regressions for the vendored verilog-pcie MSI-X core.

See src/templates/sv/vendor/verilog-pcie/README.md (MX-02).
"""

import hashlib
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from pcie_msix_local_patches import HOST_PORT_HUNKS, LIVE_CONTROL_HUNKS

VENDOR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/templates/sv/vendor/verilog-pcie"
CORE = VENDOR / "pcie_msix.v"
UPSTREAM_SHA256 = "85da9abfe32cc3ca92934ac9ae2c1228da606496e8762a9015766791410d9570"

# Every local modification as (fix id, vendored text, upstream text). Reverting
# all of them must reproduce the pinned upstream file byte for byte; reverting
# one fix lets a test prove its regression detects that defect.
PATCHES = [
    (
        "provenance",
        "// Vendored from https://github.com/alexforencich/verilog-pcie\n"
        "// revision 25156a9a162c41c60f11f41590c7d006d015ae5a, rtl/pcie_msix.v.\n"
        "// Local modifications (see README.md in this directory):\n"
        "//   MX-02: default PBA write address uses >> 6 (64-bit PBA words), was >> 5.\n"
        "//   MX-02b: scan re-reads the PBA word after any PBA write (stale-word fix);\n"
        "//           masked branch advances the scan index (head-of-line fix);\n"
        "//           Vector Control Mask bits reset to 1 (PCIe default).\n"
        "//   MX-04: a single-clock host port and a duplicated table replace the\n"
        "//          AXI-lite slave (one host read and one host write every clock).\n"
        "//   MX-05: msix_clear sweep, Bus Master Enable gating, a commit/withdraw\n"
        "//          contract for presented messages, requests dropped while disabled,\n"
        "//          and scan fairness under continuous requests.\n"
        "\n",
        "",
    ),
    (
        "pba_addr",
        "    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_reg >> 6; "
        "// MX-02: PBA words are 64 bits; upstream used >> 5\n",
        "    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_reg >> 5;\n",
    ),
    (
        "stale_word",
        "reg [63:0] pba_mem_rd_data_reg = 0;\n"
        "// MX-02b: pba_mem_rd_data_reg holds the PBA word for irq_index_reg's group\n"
        "reg pba_word_valid_reg = 1'b0, pba_word_valid_next;\n",
        "reg [63:0] pba_mem_rd_data_reg = 0;\n",
    ),
    (
        "stale_word",
        "                if (!pba_word_valid_reg) begin\n"
        "                    // MX-02b: cached word was invalidated by a PBA write; refresh it\n"
        "                    pba_mem_rd_en = 1'b1;\n"
        "                    pba_mem_addr = irq_index_reg >> 6;\n"
        "\n"
        "                    state_next = STATE_IDLE;\n"
        "                end else if (pba_mem_rd_data_reg[irq_index_reg & 6'h3f]) begin\n",
        "                if (pba_mem_rd_data_reg[irq_index_reg & 6'h3f]) begin\n",
    ),
    (
        "stale_word",
        "    endcase\n"
        "\n"
        "    // MX-02b: a PBA write invalidates the cached word; a read refreshes it\n"
        "    pba_word_valid_next = pba_mem_wr_en ? 1'b0 : "
        "(pba_mem_rd_en ? 1'b1 : pba_word_valid_reg);\n",
        "    endcase\n",
    ),
    (
        "stale_word",
        "    irq_index_reg <= irq_index_next;\n"
        "    pba_word_valid_reg <= pba_word_valid_next;\n",
        "    irq_index_reg <= irq_index_next;\n",
    ),
    (
        "stale_word",
        "        state_reg <= STATE_IDLE;\n" "        pba_word_valid_reg <= 1'b0;\n",
        "        state_reg <= STATE_IDLE;\n",
    ),
    (
        "masked_advance",
        "                // MX-02b: move past a still-masked vector so the scan cannot livelock on it\n"
        "                irq_index_next = irq_index_reg + 1;\n",
        "",
    ),
    (
        "mask_default",
        "        // MX-02b: odd words hold Vector Control; its Mask bit defaults to 1\n"
        "        tbl_mem[i] = (i & 1) ? 64'h0000000100000000 : 64'd0;\n",
        "        tbl_mem[i] = 0;\n",
    ),
]
# Later layers are recorded against the text before them, so they are listed
# (and reverted) newest first, after the provenance comment.
PATCHES = (
    PATCHES[:1]
    + [("live_control", local, upstream) for local, upstream in LIVE_CONTROL_HUNKS]
    + [("host_port", local, upstream) for local, upstream in HOST_PORT_HUNKS]
    + PATCHES[1:]
)
FIX_IDS = {"pba_addr", "stale_word", "masked_advance", "mask_default"}


def revert(fixes):
    """Undo the named modifications. MX-02 fixes can be reverted alone because
    no later layer touches their text; later layers revert newest first."""
    text = CORE.read_text()
    for fix, local, upstream in PATCHES:
        if fix in fixes:
            assert text.count(local) == 1, f"{fix} patch not found exactly once"
            text = text.replace(local, upstream)
    return text


def upstream_text():
    return revert({fix for fix, _, _ in PATCHES})


def test_vendored_core_is_upstream_plus_recorded_patches():
    digest = hashlib.sha256(upstream_text().encode()).hexdigest()
    assert digest == UPSTREAM_SHA256


def test_vendored_core_retains_mit_notice():
    header = CORE.read_text()[:1200]
    assert "Copyright (c) 2022 Alex Forencich" in header
    assert "Permission is hereby granted, free of charge" in header
    assert "Permission is hereby granted" in (VENDOR / "LICENSE").read_text()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- simulation

MSG_ADDR = 0xFEE00000  # x86 LAPIC message window; 32-bit, so 3DW MWr
MSG_ADDR64 = 0x00000001FEE00000  # above 4 GiB, so 4DW MWr
REQUESTER_ID = 0x0100


def msg_data(idx):
    return 0x4100 + idx


TB = r"""
`timescale 1ns/1ps
module tb;
localparam W = __WIDTH__;
localparam AW = W + 5;
localparam NVEC = 1 << W;
localparam NWORDS = (NVEC + 63) / 64;
localparam [AW-1:0] PBA = 1 << (AW - 1);

reg clk = 0, rst = 1;
always #2 clk = ~clk;

reg [AW-1:0] awaddr = 0, araddr = 0;
reg [31:0] wdata = 0;
reg [3:0] wstrb = 4'hf;
reg awvalid = 0, wvalid = 0, arvalid = 0;
wire awready, wready, bvalid, arready, rvalid;
wire [1:0] bresp, rresp;
wire [31:0] rdata;
reg [W-1:0] irq_index = 0;
reg irq_valid = 0;
wire irq_ready;
wire [31:0] tlp_data;
wire tlp_strb, tlp_valid, tlp_sop, tlp_eop;
wire [127:0] tlp_hdr;
reg msix_enable = 0, msix_mask = 0;
reg tx_ready = 1;

`ifdef HOST_PORT
reg hwv = 0, hwp = 0, hrv = 0, hrp = 0;
reg bme = 1, clr = 0;
wire clearing;
reg [W+1:0] hwdw = 0, hrdw = 0;
reg [31:0] hwd = 0;
wire [31:0] hrd;
pcie_msix #(.IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH(W), .TLP_HDR_WIDTH(128), .TLP_FORCE_64_BIT_ADDR(0)) dut (
  .clk(clk), .rst(rst),
  .host_wr_valid(hwv), .host_wr_pba(hwp), .host_wr_dw(hwdw), .host_wr_data(hwd), .host_wr_be(wstrb),
  .host_rd_valid(hrv), .host_rd_pba(hrp), .host_rd_dw(hrdw), .host_rd_data(hrd),
  .irq_index(irq_index), .irq_valid(irq_valid), .irq_ready(irq_ready),
  .tx_wr_req_tlp_data(tlp_data), .tx_wr_req_tlp_strb(tlp_strb), .tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr(tlp_hdr),
  .tx_wr_req_tlp_valid(tlp_valid), .tx_wr_req_tlp_sop(tlp_sop), .tx_wr_req_tlp_eop(tlp_eop),
  .tx_wr_req_tlp_ready(tx_ready),
  .requester_id(16'h__RID__), .msix_enable(msix_enable), .msix_mask(msix_mask),
  .bus_master_enable(bme), .msix_clear(clr), .msix_clearing(clearing));
`else
pcie_msix #(.IRQ_INDEX_WIDTH(W), .AXIL_DATA_WIDTH(32), .AXIL_ADDR_WIDTH(AW),
            .AXIL_STRB_WIDTH(4), .TLP_HDR_WIDTH(128), .TLP_FORCE_64_BIT_ADDR(0)) dut (
  .clk(clk), .rst(rst),
  .s_axil_awaddr(awaddr), .s_axil_awprot(3'b0), .s_axil_awvalid(awvalid), .s_axil_awready(awready),
  .s_axil_wdata(wdata), .s_axil_wstrb(wstrb), .s_axil_wvalid(wvalid), .s_axil_wready(wready),
  .s_axil_bresp(bresp), .s_axil_bvalid(bvalid), .s_axil_bready(1'b1),
  .s_axil_araddr(araddr), .s_axil_arprot(3'b0), .s_axil_arvalid(arvalid), .s_axil_arready(arready),
  .s_axil_rdata(rdata), .s_axil_rresp(rresp), .s_axil_rvalid(rvalid), .s_axil_rready(1'b1),
  .irq_index(irq_index), .irq_valid(irq_valid), .irq_ready(irq_ready),
  .tx_wr_req_tlp_data(tlp_data), .tx_wr_req_tlp_strb(tlp_strb), .tx_wr_req_tlp_hdr(tlp_hdr),
  .tx_wr_req_tlp_valid(tlp_valid), .tx_wr_req_tlp_sop(tlp_sop), .tx_wr_req_tlp_eop(tlp_eop),
  .tx_wr_req_tlp_ready(tx_ready),
  .requester_id(16'h__RID__), .msix_enable(msix_enable), .msix_mask(msix_mask));
`endif

// Captured message-write TLPs, accepted on valid && ready.
reg [127:0] cap_hdr [0:63];
reg [31:0] cap_data [0:63];
integer cap_n = 0, cap_rd = 0;
always @(posedge clk) if (tlp_valid && tx_ready) begin
  if (cap_n >= 64) $fatal(1, "message TLP storm: more than 64 captured");
  cap_hdr[cap_n] <= tlp_hdr; cap_data[cap_n] <= tlp_data; cap_n <= cap_n + 1;
end

// Testbench drives and samples on negedges so handshakes never race the DUT.
// Addresses use the upstream AXI-lite map (PBA at the top half) on both ports.
`ifdef HOST_PORT
task wr32(input [AW-1:0] a, input [31:0] d);
  begin
    @(negedge clk); hwp = a[AW-1]; hwdw = (a & ~PBA) >> 2; hwd = d; hwv = 1;
    @(negedge clk); hwv = 0;
  end
endtask

task rd32(input [AW-1:0] a, output [31:0] d);
  begin
    @(negedge clk); hrp = a[AW-1]; hrdw = (a & ~PBA) >> 2; hrv = 1;
    @(negedge clk); hrv = 0;
    @(negedge clk); d = hrd;  // fixed two-clock latency
  end
endtask
`else
task wr32(input [AW-1:0] a, input [31:0] d);
  begin
    @(negedge clk); awaddr = a; wdata = d; awvalid = 1; wvalid = 1;
    while (!awready) @(negedge clk);
    awvalid = 0; wvalid = 0;
  end
endtask

task rd32(input [AW-1:0] a, output [31:0] d);
  begin
    @(negedge clk); araddr = a; arvalid = 1;
    while (!arready) @(negedge clk);
    arvalid = 0;
    while (!rvalid) @(negedge clk);
    d = rdata;
  end
endtask
`endif

task rd64(input [AW-1:0] a, output [63:0] d);
  reg [31:0] lo, hi;
  begin rd32(a, lo); rd32(a + 4, hi); d = {hi, lo}; end
endtask

task prog_vec(input integer idx, input [63:0] addr, input masked);
  begin
    wr32(idx * 16 + 0, addr[31:0]);
    wr32(idx * 16 + 4, addr[63:32]);
    wr32(idx * 16 + 8, 32'h4100 + idx);
    wr32(idx * 16 + 12, masked ? 32'd1 : 32'd0);
  end
endtask

task raise(input integer idx);
  begin
    @(negedge clk); irq_index = idx; irq_valid = 1;
    while (!irq_ready) @(negedge clk);
    @(negedge clk); irq_valid = 0;
  end
endtask

task settle;
  integer k;
  begin for (k = 0; k < 40; k = k + 1) @(negedge clk); end
endtask

// Every PBA word must equal the expectation: only the listed vectors pending.
task expect_pba(input integer a, input integer b, input [255:0] what);
  integer w;
  reg [63:0] got, want;
  begin
    for (w = 0; w < NWORDS; w = w + 1) begin
      want = 64'd0;
      if (a >= 0 && a / 64 == w) want = want | (64'd1 << (a % 64));
      if (b >= 0 && b / 64 == w) want = want | (64'd1 << (b % 64));
      rd64(PBA + w * 8, got);
      if (got !== want)
        $fatal(1, "%0s: PBA word %0d got %h want %h", what, w, got, want);
    end
  end
endtask

task expect_msg(input integer idx, input [63:0] addr);
  reg [127:0] h;
  reg [63:0] a;
  integer k;
  begin
    for (k = 0; k < 200 && cap_rd >= cap_n; k = k + 1) @(negedge clk);
    if (cap_rd >= cap_n) $fatal(1, "vector %0d: no message TLP", idx);
    h = cap_hdr[cap_rd]; cap_rd = cap_rd + 1;
    a = (h[127:125] == 3'b011) ? {h[63:2], 2'b00} : {32'd0, h[63:34], 2'b00};
    if (h[124:120] !== 5'b00000 || h[127:126] !== 2'b01)
      $fatal(1, "vector %0d: not a memory write, fmt/type %b", idx, h[127:120]);
    if ((addr >> 32) != 0 && h[127:125] !== 3'b011)
      $fatal(1, "vector %0d: 64-bit address sent as 3DW", idx);
    if ((addr >> 32) == 0 && h[127:125] !== 3'b010)
      $fatal(1, "vector %0d: address below 4 GiB must use a 3DW header", idx);
    if (a !== addr) $fatal(1, "vector %0d: address %h want %h", idx, a, addr);
    if (h[105:96] !== 10'd1 || h[67:64] !== 4'hf || h[71:68] !== 4'h0)
      $fatal(1, "vector %0d: length/BE %h", idx, h[105:64]);
    if (h[95:80] !== 16'h__RID__) $fatal(1, "vector %0d: requester id %h", idx, h[95:80]);
    if (cap_data[cap_rd - 1] !== 32'h4100 + idx)
      $fatal(1, "vector %0d: data %h", idx, cap_data[cap_rd - 1]);
  end
endtask

task expect_no_msg(input [255:0] what);
  begin
    if (cap_rd != cap_n)
      $fatal(1, "%0s: unexpected message TLP hdr %h data %h", what, cap_hdr[cap_rd], cap_data[cap_rd]);
  end
endtask

reg [31:0] r32;
integer k5;
initial begin
  repeat (4) @(negedge clk); rst = 0; repeat (4) @(negedge clk);
__BODY__
  // No case may leave a late or spurious message behind.
  settle; expect_no_msg("end of test");
  $display("PASS"); $finish;
end
initial begin #2000000; $fatal(1, "timeout"); end
endmodule
"""


def simulate(tmp_path, width, body, core=CORE):
    compiler, runner = shutil.which("iverilog"), shutil.which("vvp")
    if not compiler or not runner:
        pytest.skip("iverilog/vvp is not installed")
    tb = tmp_path / "tb.sv"
    tb.write_text(
        TB.replace("__WIDTH__", str(width))
        .replace("__RID__", f"{REQUESTER_ID:04x}")
        .replace("__BODY__", body)
    )
    out = tmp_path / "sim.vvp"
    defines = ["-DHOST_PORT"] if "host_wr_valid" in Path(core).read_text() else []
    compiled = subprocess.run(
        [compiler, "-g2012", *defines, "-s", "tb", "-o", str(out), str(core), str(tb)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=60,
    )
    assert compiled.returncode == 0, compiled.stdout + compiled.stderr
    return subprocess.run(
        [runner, str(out)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120
    )


def assert_pass(result):
    assert result.returncode == 0 and "PASS" in result.stdout, (
        result.stdout + result.stderr
    )


def masked_roundtrip(idx):
    return f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec({idx}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + idx * 4:x}, 1);
  raise({idx}); settle;
  expect_no_msg("masked vector {idx}");
  expect_pba({idx}, -1, "after masked irq {idx}");
  wr32({idx} * 16 + 12, 0);
  expect_msg({idx}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + idx * 4:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "after delivering {idx}");
"""


def delivery_preserves(idx, victim):
    return f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec({victim}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + victim * 4:x}, 1);
  prog_vec({idx}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + idx * 4:x}, 0);
  raise({victim}); settle;
  expect_pba({victim}, -1, "victim {victim} pending");
  raise({idx});
  expect_msg({idx}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + idx * 4:x}); settle;
  expect_pba({victim}, -1, "after delivering {idx}, victim {victim}");
"""


MASKED_CASES = sorted(
    {
        (w, i)
        for w in (6, 7, 11)
        for i in (0, 31, 32, 63, 64, (1 << w) - 1)
        if i < (1 << w)
    }
)
DELIVERY_CASES = [(7, 32, 70), (11, 32, 70), (11, 100, 200), (7, 5, 33), (6, 40, 3)]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("width,idx", MASKED_CASES)
def test_masked_vector_sets_and_clears_its_own_pba_bit(tmp_path, width, idx):
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, width, masked_roundtrip(idx)))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("width,idx,victim", DELIVERY_CASES)
def test_delivery_preserves_other_pending_vectors(tmp_path, width, idx, victim):
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, width, delivery_preserves(idx, victim)))


def head_of_line():
    """A still-masked pending vector must not block delivery of another one.

    Vector 0 is raised first, so the scan finds it and parks there (requests
    do not move the scan since MX-05); vector 5 is then raised and unmasked.
    """
    return f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(0, 64'h{MSG_ADDR:x}, 1); prog_vec(5, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 20:x}, 1);
  raise(0); settle; raise(5); settle;
  expect_pba(0, 5, "both pending");
  wr32(5 * 16 + 12, 0);
  expect_msg(5, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 20:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(0, -1, "vector 0 still masked and pending");
"""


def group_boundary(delivered, pending):
    """Delivering the last vector of a group must not reuse the old PBA word."""
    return f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec({pending}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + pending * 4:x}, 1);
  prog_vec({delivered}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + delivered * 4:x}, 0);
  raise({pending}); settle;
  raise({delivered});
  expect_msg({delivered}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + delivered * 4:x}); settle;
  expect_no_msg("after delivering {delivered}");
  expect_pba({pending}, -1, "only {pending} pending");
"""


def group_boundary_scan(delivered, pending):
    """The scan, not a request, delivers the last vector of a group and must
    re-read the PBA word before testing the first vector of the next group."""
    return f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec({pending}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + pending * 4:x}, 1);
  prog_vec({delivered}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + delivered * 4:x}, 1);
  raise({pending}); raise({delivered}); settle;
  expect_pba({pending}, {delivered}, "both pending");
  wr32({delivered} * 16 + 12, 0);
  expect_msg({delivered}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + delivered * 4:x}); settle;
  expect_no_msg("after the scan delivered {delivered}");
  expect_pba({pending}, -1, "only {pending} pending");
"""


def unprogrammed():
    """A vector the host never wrote must stay masked (PCIe default Mask=1)."""
    return """
  msix_enable = 1;
  raise(7); settle;
  expect_no_msg("unprogrammed vector 7");
  expect_pba(7, -1, "unprogrammed vector 7 pending");
"""


def test_scan_does_not_livelock_on_a_masked_pending_vector(tmp_path):
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, head_of_line()))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("delivered,pending", [(63, 0), (127, 64), (63, 64)])
def test_scan_rereads_pba_after_crossing_a_group(tmp_path, delivered, pending):
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 7, group_boundary(delivered, pending)))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("delivered,pending", [(63, 0), (127, 64)])
def test_scan_delivery_rereads_pba_after_crossing_a_group(tmp_path, delivered, pending):
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 7, group_boundary_scan(delivered, pending)))


def test_unprogrammed_vector_is_masked_by_default(tmp_path):
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, unprogrammed()))


# Each local fix, reverted alone, must make its regression fail with this symptom.
SENSITIVITY = [
    ("pba_addr", 7, masked_roundtrip(32), "after masked irq 32: PBA word 0 got"),
    ("stale_word", 7, group_boundary_scan(63, 0), "PBA word 1 got"),
    ("masked_advance", 6, head_of_line(), "vector 5: no message TLP"),
    (
        "mask_default",
        6,
        unprogrammed(),
        "unprogrammed vector 7: unexpected message TLP",
    ),
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "fix,width,body,symptom", SENSITIVITY, ids=[s[0] for s in SENSITIVITY]
)
def test_each_fix_is_detected_when_reverted(tmp_path, fix, width, body, symptom):
    assert {s[0] for s in SENSITIVITY} == FIX_IDS
    core = tmp_path / f"pcie_msix_without_{fix}.v"
    core.write_text(revert({fix}))
    result = simulate(tmp_path, width, body, core=core)
    output = result.stdout + result.stderr
    assert result.returncode != 0 and "PASS" not in result.stdout, output
    assert symptom in output, output


def test_pristine_upstream_writes_to_host_address_zero(tmp_path):
    upstream = tmp_path / "pcie_msix_upstream.v"
    upstream.write_text(upstream_text())
    result = simulate(tmp_path, 7, masked_roundtrip(32), core=upstream)
    assert result.returncode != 0 and "PASS" not in result.stdout
    # The misplaced pending bit (word 1 bit 32, vector 96) is scanned and
    # "delivered" from an unprogrammed, unmasked-by-default table entry: a 3DW
    # MWr of 0 to host address 0 while the requested vector is still masked.
    spurious = (
        "unexpected message TLP hdr 400000010100000f0000000000000000 data 00000000"
    )
    assert spurious in result.stdout + result.stderr, result.stdout + result.stderr


def test_function_mask_defers_then_delivers(tmp_path):
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1; msix_mask = 1;
  prog_vec(9, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 36:x}, 0);
  raise(9); settle;
  expect_no_msg("function masked");
  expect_pba(9, -1, "function masked");
  msix_mask = 0;
  expect_msg(9, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 36:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "function unmasked");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_64_bit_message_address_uses_4dw_header(tmp_path):
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(2, 64'h{MSG_ADDR64:x}, 0);
  raise(2);
  expect_msg(2, 64'h{MSG_ADDR64:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "after 4DW delivery");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_stalled_message_is_held_stable_and_sent_once(tmp_path):
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}, 0);
  @(negedge clk); tx_ready = 0;
  raise(6);
  while (!tlp_valid) @(negedge clk);
  r32 = tlp_data;
  repeat (25) begin
    @(negedge clk);
    if (!tlp_valid || tlp_data !== r32) $fatal(1, "stalled message dropped or changed");
  end
  expect_no_msg("while stalled");
  tx_ready = 1;
  expect_msg(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "after stalled delivery");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_request_while_msix_disabled_is_dropped(tmp_path):
    """MX-05 contract: requests while MSI-X Enable is clear are not recorded, so
    a driver enabling MSI-X later does not receive events from before."""
    body = f"""
  prog_vec(4, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 16:x}, 0);
  raise(4); settle;
  expect_no_msg("msix disabled");
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "msix disabled");
  msix_enable = 1; settle;
  expect_no_msg("nothing delivered on enable");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_rst_preserves_table_and_pba(tmp_path):
    """MX-05 contract: rst includes PCILeech's own soft reset, which is not a
    PCIe reset, so it must not wipe state the host driver programmed."""
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(3, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 12:x}, 1);
  raise(3); settle;
  expect_pba(3, -1, "before reset");
  @(negedge clk); rst = 1; repeat (4) @(negedge clk); rst = 0; repeat (4) @(negedge clk);
  expect_pba(3, -1, "after rst (pending survives)");
  rd32(3 * 16 + 0, r32);
  if (r32 !== 32'h{MSG_ADDR + 12:x}) $fatal(1, "rst changed the table: %h", r32);
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ MX-05

CLEAR_CHECK = """
  // Every entry is back at its reset value and nothing is pending.
  for (k5 = 0; k5 < NVEC; k5 = k5 + 1) begin
    rd32(k5 * 16 + 0, r32); if (r32 !== 0) $fatal(1, "entry %0d address %h after clear", k5, r32);
    rd32(k5 * 16 + 8, r32); if (r32 !== 0) $fatal(1, "entry %0d data %h after clear", k5, r32);
    rd32(k5 * 16 + 12, r32); if (r32 !== 1) $fatal(1, "entry %0d control %h after clear", k5, r32);
  end
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "after clear");
"""


@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [6, 7, 11])
def test_msix_clear_restores_reset_values_and_drops_writes_meanwhile(tmp_path, width):
    top = (1 << width) - 1
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(2, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 8:x}, 0);
  prog_vec({top}, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 4:x}, 1);
  raise({top}); settle;
  expect_pba({top}, -1, "before clear");
  @(negedge clk); clr = 1; @(negedge clk); clr = 0;
  if (!clearing) $fatal(1, "clear sweep did not start");
  if (irq_ready) $fatal(1, "requests accepted during the clear sweep");
  repeat (4) @(negedge clk);   // the sweep has passed entry 0 by now
  wr32(0 * 16 + 8, 32'hdead);  // dropped: the sweep owns the table
  while (clearing) @(negedge clk);
{CLEAR_CHECK}
  // The vector that was unmasked before the clear is masked again.
  raise(2); settle;
  expect_no_msg("vector 2 after clear");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, width, body.replace("NVEC", "NVEC")))


def test_clear_requested_during_rst_completes_after_rst(tmp_path):
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(5, 64'h{MSG_ADDR:x}, 1);
  raise(5); settle;
  @(negedge clk); rst = 1; clr = 1; repeat (3) @(negedge clk);
  clr = 0; repeat (2) @(negedge clk); rst = 0;
  @(negedge clk); while (clearing) @(negedge clk);
{CLEAR_CHECK}
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_clear_withdraws_a_presented_message(tmp_path):
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}, 0);
  @(negedge clk); tx_ready = 0;
  raise(6);
  while (!tlp_valid) @(negedge clk);
  @(negedge clk); clr = 1; @(negedge clk); clr = 0;
  if (tlp_valid) $fatal(1, "presented message survived the clear");
  tx_ready = 1; while (clearing) @(negedge clk);
  settle; expect_no_msg("after clear");
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "after clear");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "control,off,on",
    [
        ("function_mask", "msix_mask = 1", "msix_mask = 0"),
        ("bus_master", "bme = 0", "bme = 1"),
    ],
)
def test_presented_message_is_withdrawn_and_repended_then_sent_once(
    tmp_path, control, off, on
):
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}, 0);
  @(negedge clk); tx_ready = 0;
  raise(6);
  while (!tlp_valid) @(negedge clk);
  @(negedge clk); {off};
  repeat (3) @(negedge clk);
  if (tlp_valid) $fatal(1, "{control}: message still presented");
  expect_pba(6, -1, "{control}: withdrawn message is pending");
  tx_ready = 1; settle;
  expect_no_msg("{control}: while off");
  {on};
  expect_msg(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "{control}: delivered once");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [3, 6, 7])
def test_back_to_back_requests_with_an_empty_pba(tmp_path, width):
    """Regression: with <= 64 vectors an empty-group scan step does not move
    the index, which once left the scan turn owed forever and blocked every
    request after the first."""
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(1, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 4:x}, 0);
  prog_vec(2, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 8:x}, 0);
  raise(1); expect_msg(1, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 4:x});
  raise(2); expect_msg(2, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 8:x});
  raise(1); expect_msg(1, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 4:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "all delivered");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, width, body))


def test_scanned_vector_keeps_its_pending_bit_when_disabled_mid_presentation(tmp_path):
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}, 1);
  raise(6); settle;
  expect_pba(6, -1, "pending while masked");
  @(negedge clk); tx_ready = 0;
  wr32(6 * 16 + 12, 0);             // unmask: the scan presents it
  while (!tlp_valid) @(negedge clk);
  @(negedge clk); msix_enable = 0;
  repeat (3) @(negedge clk);
  if (tlp_valid) $fatal(1, "message still presented after disable");
  tx_ready = 1; settle;
  expect_no_msg("disabled");
  expect_pba(6, -1, "scanned vector still pending after disable");
  msix_enable = 1;
  expect_msg(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "delivered on re-enable");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_controls_dropping_before_presentation_never_present(tmp_path):
    """Function mask set in the clocks between the table read and presentation:
    the message must not be presented, and must stay pending."""
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}, 0);
  @(negedge clk); irq_index = 6; irq_valid = 1;
  while (!irq_ready) @(negedge clk);
  @(negedge clk); irq_valid = 0;
  while (dut.state_reg !== 3'd2) @(negedge clk);  // READ_TBL_2 decides to send
  msix_mask = 1;                      // registered in time for SEND_TLP
  repeat (6) @(negedge clk);
  expect_no_msg("masked before presentation");
  expect_pba(6, -1, "pending after masked presentation");
  msix_mask = 0;
  expect_msg(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}); settle;
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_presented_message_is_dropped_when_msix_is_disabled(tmp_path):
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(6, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 24:x}, 0);
  @(negedge clk); tx_ready = 0;
  raise(6);
  while (!tlp_valid) @(negedge clk);
  @(negedge clk); msix_enable = 0;
  repeat (3) @(negedge clk);
  if (tlp_valid) $fatal(1, "message still presented after disable");
  tx_ready = 1; settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "dropped, not pending");
  msix_enable = 1; settle;
  expect_no_msg("dropped message is not delivered on re-enable");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_bus_master_disable_holds_requests_pending(tmp_path):
    body = f"""

  prog_vec(9, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 36:x}, 0);
  raise(9); settle;
  expect_no_msg("bus mastering off");
  expect_pba(9, -1, "bus mastering off");
  bme = 1;
  expect_msg(9, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 36:x}); settle;
  expect_pba(-1, -1, "bus mastering on");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_continuous_requests_cannot_starve_a_pending_vector(tmp_path):
    """A producer holding irq_valid high (here on a masked vector) must not stop
    the scan from delivering another vector once it is unmasked."""
    body = f"""
  msix_enable = 1;
  prog_vec(0, 64'h{MSG_ADDR:x}, 1);
  prog_vec(1, 64'h{MSG_ADDR + 4:x}, 1);
  raise(0); settle;
  @(negedge clk); irq_index = 1; irq_valid = 1;
  repeat (20) @(negedge clk);
  wr32(0 * 16 + 12, 0);
  expect_msg(0, 64'h{MSG_ADDR:x});
  @(negedge clk); irq_valid = 0; settle;
  expect_pba(1, -1, "vector 1 still masked and pending");
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))


def test_known_behavior_vector_control_reserved_bits_are_stored(tmp_path):
    """Pins upstream behavior for MX-05; reserved-bit readback is undecided."""
    body = """
  wr32(12, 32'hffffffff);
  rd32(12, r32);
  if (r32 !== 32'hffffffff) $fatal(1, "vector control readback %h", r32);
"""
    assert_pass(simulate(tmp_path, 6, body))
```

```py
"""Test script to verify version checking functionality."""

import os
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

import pytest

from pcileechfwgenerator.__version__ import __version__
from pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker import (check_and_notify, check_for_updates,
                                     fetch_latest_version, is_newer_version,
                                     parse_version)


class TestVersionParsing:
    """Test version parsing functionality."""

    def test_parse_version_basic(self):
        """Test basic version parsing."""
        assert parse_version("0.5.8") == (0, 5, 8)
        assert parse_version("1.2.3") == (1, 2, 3)
        assert parse_version("10.20.30") == (10, 20, 30)

    def test_parse_version_with_v_prefix(self):
        """Test parsing versions with 'v' prefix."""
        assert parse_version("v0.5.8") == (0, 5, 8)
        assert parse_version("v1.2.3") == (1, 2, 3)

    def test_parse_version_invalid(self):
        """Test parsing invalid versions."""
        assert parse_version("invalid") == (0, 0, 0)
        assert parse_version("") == (0, 0, 0)


class TestVersionComparison:
    """Test version comparison functionality."""

    def test_is_newer_version_newer(self):
        """Test detecting newer versions."""
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.7", "0.5.8") is True
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.8", "0.6.0") is True
        assert is_newer_version("0.9.9", "1.0.0") is True

    def test_is_newer_version_same(self):
        """Test same version comparison."""
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.8", "0.5.8") is False
        assert is_newer_version("1.0.0", "1.0.0") is False

    def test_is_newer_version_older(self):
        """Test detecting older versions."""
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.8", "0.5.7") is False
        assert is_newer_version("1.0.0", "0.9.9") is False

    def test_is_newer_version_with_prefix(self):
        """Test version comparison with v prefix."""
        assert is_newer_version("v0.5.7", "v0.5.8") is True
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.7", "v0.5.8") is True
        assert is_newer_version("v0.5.8", "0.5.7") is False


class TestNonBlockingBehavior:
    """Test that version checking never blocks the main program."""

    @patch("pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker.fetch_latest_version")
    def test_network_failure_does_not_block(self, mock_fetch):
        """Test that network failures don't block execution."""
        mock_fetch.side_effect = Exception("Network error")

        # Should return None without raising
        result = check_for_updates(force=True)
        assert result is None

    @patch("pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker.urlopen")
    def test_timeout_does_not_block(self, mock_urlopen):
        """Test that timeouts don't block execution."""
        mock_urlopen.side_effect = TimeoutError("Request timed out")

        # Should return None without raising
        result = fetch_latest_version()
        assert result is None

    @patch("pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker.check_for_updates")
    @patch("pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker.prompt_for_update")
    def test_check_and_notify_handles_errors(self, mock_prompt, mock_check):
        """Test that check_and_notify handles all errors gracefully."""
        # Test with various error scenarios
        test_cases = [
            Exception("Generic error"),
            ValueError("Invalid value"),
            KeyError("Missing key"),
            None,  # No error, but no update
        ]

        for error in test_cases:
            if error:
                mock_check.side_effect = error
            else:
                mock_check.return_value = None

            # Should not raise any exception
            try:
                check_and_notify()
            except Exception as e:
                pytest.fail(f"check_and_notify raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

    def test_cache_write_failure_does_not_block(self):
        """Test that cache write failures don't block execution."""
        from pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker import save_cache

        # Mock the CACHE_FILE to raise permission error
        with patch("pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker.CACHE_FILE") as mock_cache_file:
            mock_cache_file.parent.mkdir.side_effect = PermissionError("No permission")

            # Should handle gracefully without raising
            try:
                save_cache("1.0.0", True)
                # Function should complete without raising
            except Exception as e:
                pytest.fail(f"save_cache raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}")


class TestIntegration:
    """Integration tests for version checking."""

    @patch("pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker.fetch_latest_version")
    @patch.dict(os.environ, {"CI": "", "PCILEECH_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK": ""}, clear=True)
    def test_update_available_flow(self, mock_fetch):
        """Test the flow when an update is available."""
        mock_fetch.return_value = "99.0.0"  # Much newer version

        result = check_for_updates(force=True)
        assert result is not None
        latest_version, update_available = result
        assert latest_version == "99.0.0"
        assert update_available is True

    @patch("pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker.fetch_latest_version")
    @patch.dict(os.environ, {"CI": "", "PCILEECH_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK": ""}, clear=True)
    def test_no_update_needed_flow(self, mock_fetch):
        """Test the flow when no update is needed."""
        mock_fetch.return_value = __version__  # Same version

        result = check_for_updates(force=True)
        assert result is not None
        latest_version, update_available = result
        assert latest_version == __version__
        assert update_available is False
```

```py
"""Tests for version checker functionality."""

import json
import os
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import Mock, mock_open, patch

import pytest

from pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker import (CACHE_FILE, check_for_updates,
                                     fetch_latest_version_github,
                                     fetch_latest_version_pypi,
                                     get_cached_check, is_newer_version,
                                     parse_version, save_cache)


class TestVersionParsing:
    """Test version parsing and comparison."""

    def test_parse_version_basic(self):
        """Test basic version parsing."""
        assert parse_version("1.2.3") == (1, 2, 3)
        assert parse_version("0.5.8") == (0, 5, 8)
        assert parse_version("10.20.30") == (10, 20, 30)

    def test_parse_version_with_v_prefix(self):
        """Test parsing versions with 'v' prefix."""
        assert parse_version("v1.2.3") == (1, 2, 3)
        assert parse_version("v0.5.8") == (0, 5, 8)

    def test_parse_version_invalid(self):
        """Test parsing invalid versions."""
        assert parse_version("invalid") == (0, 0, 0)
        assert parse_version("") == (0, 0, 0)
        # Test with a non-string type converted to string
        assert parse_version(str(None)) == (0, 0, 0)

    def test_is_newer_version(self):
        """Test version comparison."""
        # Newer versions
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.7", "0.5.8") is True
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.8", "0.6.0") is True
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.8", "1.0.0") is True

        # Same version
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.8", "0.5.8") is False

        # Older versions
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.8", "0.5.7") is False
        assert is_newer_version("1.0.0", "0.9.9") is False

        # With v prefix
        assert is_newer_version("v0.5.7", "v0.5.8") is True
        assert is_newer_version("0.5.7", "v0.5.8") is True


class TestCaching:
    """Test version check caching."""

    def test_get_cached_check_no_file(self):
        """Test getting cache when file doesn't exist."""
        with patch.object(Path, "exists", return_value=False):
            assert get_cached_check() is None

    def test_get_cached_check_fresh(self):
        """Test getting fresh cache."""
        cache_data = {
            "last_check": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "latest_version": "0.6.0",
            "current_version": "0.5.8",
            "update_available": True,
        }

        with patch.object(Path, "exists", return_value=True):
            with patch("builtins.open", mock_open(read_data=json.dumps(cache_data))):
                result = get_cached_check()
                assert result == cache_data

    def test_get_cached_check_stale(self):
        """Test getting stale cache."""
        old_date = datetime.now() - timedelta(days=2)
        cache_data = {
            "last_check": old_date.isoformat(),
            "latest_version": "0.6.0",
            "current_version": "0.5.8",
            "update_available": True,
        }

        with patch.object(Path, "exists", return_value=True):
            with patch("builtins.open", mock_open(read_data=json.dumps(cache_data))):
                assert get_cached_check() is None

    def test_save_cache(self):
        """Test saving cache."""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            cache_file = Path(tmpdir) / "version_check.json"

            with patch("pcileechfwgenerator.cli.version_checker.CACHE_FILE", cache_file):
                save_cache("0.6.0", True)

                assert cache_file.exists()
                with open(cache_file) as f:
                    data = json.load(f)

                assert data["latest_version"] == "0.6.0"
                assert data["update_available"] is True
                assert "last_check" in data
                assert "current_version" in data
```

`tests/test_vfio_access_seam.py`:

```py
"""Tests for the VFIOAccess domain seam.

The domain (ConfigSpaceManager / VFIODeviceManager) depends on a VFIOAccess
Protocol it owns, not on the concrete CLI helpers. These tests verify the
default adapter resolves and that a fake adapter can be injected so domain VFIO
logic is exercisable without root or real hardware.
"""

from pcileechfwgenerator.device_clone.config_space_manager import ConfigSpaceManager
from pcileechfwgenerator.device_clone.vfio_access import (
    VFIOAccess,
    get_default_vfio_access,
)


class _FakeBinder:
    def __init__(self):
        self.bound = False

    @property
    def is_bound(self):
        return self.bound

    def bind(self):
        self.bound = True

    def unbind(self):
        self.bound = False


class _FakeVFIOAccess:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []

    def ensure_binding(self, bdf):
        self.calls.append(("ensure_binding", bdf))
        return "42"

    def open_device(self, bdf):
        self.calls.append(("open_device", bdf))
        return (3, 4)

    def bind_for_session(self, bdf, attach=True):
        self.calls.append(("bind_for_session", bdf, attach))
        return _FakeBinder()


def test_default_adapter_satisfies_protocol():
    adapter = get_default_vfio_access()
    assert isinstance(adapter, VFIOAccess)


def test_fake_adapter_satisfies_protocol():
    assert isinstance(_FakeVFIOAccess(), VFIOAccess)


def test_config_space_manager_accepts_injected_access():
    fake = _FakeVFIOAccess()
    mgr = ConfigSpaceManager("0000:01:00.0", vfio_access=fake)
    assert mgr._vfio_access is fake


def test_config_space_manager_defaults_to_cli_adapter():
    mgr = ConfigSpaceManager("0000:01:00.0")
    assert isinstance(mgr._vfio_access, VFIOAccess)


def test_importing_vfio_access_does_not_import_cli():
    # The port module must not drag the CLI layer in at import time.
    # Fresh-ish check: the adapter only imports CLI lazily inside its methods.
    import importlib
    import sys

    importlib.import_module("pcileechfwgenerator.device_clone.vfio_access")
    # We don't assert cli is absent globally (other tests may import it), but
    # constructing the default adapter must not require CLI to be importable
    # at definition time — covered by the import succeeding above.
    assert "pcileechfwgenerator.device_clone.vfio_access" in sys.modules


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import pytest

    pytest.main([__file__, "-v"])
```

`tests/test_vfio_binder_transactions.py`:

```py
"""VFIOBinder acquisition is transactional and restoration is verified.

A stateful fake models the kernel's binding state (driver, driver_override,
vfio-pci dynamic IDs) at the binder's sysfs primitives, so failures can be
injected after each acquisition step without hardware.
"""

import pytest
from pcileechfwgenerator.cli.vfio_handler import VFIOBinder
from pcileechfwgenerator.exceptions import VFIOBindError

BDF = "0000:03:00.0"


class Kernel:
    def __init__(self, driver="e1000e", override=""):
        self.driver = driver
        self.native = driver if driver != "vfio-pci" else "e1000e"
        self.override = override
        self.vfio_ids = False
        self.locked = False
        self.fail = set()

    def check(self, step):
        if step in self.fail:
            raise OSError(f"injected failure: {step}")


def binder_for(kernel, monkeypatch, tmp_path=None):
    monkeypatch.setattr(VFIOBinder, "_validate_permissions", staticmethod(lambda: None))
    monkeypatch.setattr(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context", lambda self: None)
    binder = VFIOBinder(
        BDF, attach=False, journal_directory=tmp_path / "j" if tmp_path else None
    )
    k = kernel

    def bind_driver(driver):
        k.check("bind:" + driver)
        if k.driver is not None:
            raise OSError("device already has a driver")
        if k.override and k.override != driver:
            raise OSError("driver_override forbids " + driver)
        k.driver = driver

    def probe():
        k.check("probe")
        if k.driver is None:
            k.driver = k.override or ("vfio-pci" if k.vfio_ids else k.native)

    def unbind_current():
        k.check("unbind")
        k.driver = None

    def set_override():
        k.check("override")
        k.override = "vfio-pci"

    def bind_vfio():
        k.vfio_ids = True
        binder._added_device_ids.append(("8086", "1533"))
        k.check("bind_vfio")
        k.driver = "vfio-pci"
        binder._bound = True

    def wait_group(_group):
        k.check("group_node")

    def cleanup_ids():
        if "remove_id" in k.fail:
            return ["remove_id 8086:1533 failed: injected"]
        k.vfio_ids = False
        binder._added_device_ids.clear()
        return []

    def save_original():
        binder.original_driver = k.driver

    def acquire(_group):
        assert not k.locked
        k.locked = True

    def release():
        k.locked = False

    def write_override(value):
        k.check("restore_override")
        k.override = value

    patches = {
        "_check_iommu": lambda: None,
        "_get_iommu_group": lambda: "7",
        "_acquire_group_lock": acquire,
        "_release_group_lock": release,
        "_save_original_driver": save_original,
        "_unbind_current_driver": unbind_current,
        "_set_driver_override": set_override,
        "_bind_to_vfio": bind_vfio,
        "_wait_for_group_node": wait_group,
        "_cleanup_device_ids": cleanup_ids,
        "_current_driver": lambda: k.driver,
        "_read_override": lambda: k.override,
        "_write_override": write_override,
        "_unbind_driver": lambda: setattr(k, "driver", None),
        "_bind_driver": bind_driver,
        "_probe_driver": probe,
    }
    for name, fn in patches.items():
        monkeypatch.setattr(binder, name, fn)
    return binder


def test_round_trip_restores_and_verifies(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    k = Kernel()
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    with binder:
        assert k.driver == "vfio-pci" and k.locked
        assert (tmp_path / "j").exists() and any((tmp_path / "j").iterdir())
    assert (k.driver, k.override, k.vfio_ids, k.locked) == ("e1000e", "", False, False)
    assert binder.final_driver == "e1000e"
    assert not any((tmp_path / "j").iterdir())  # journal cleared after verify


@pytest.mark.parametrize("step", ["unbind", "override", "bind_vfio", "group_node"])
def test_failure_after_each_step_rolls_back(monkeypatch, tmp_path, step):
    """The review's scenario: bind() fails after changing the binding; __exit__
    never runs, so bind() itself must restore the original driver."""
    k = Kernel()
    k.fail.add(step)
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(Exception, match="injected failure"):
        with binder:
            pytest.fail("body must not run")
    assert (k.driver, k.override, k.vfio_ids, k.locked) == ("e1000e", "", False, False)
    assert not any((tmp_path / "j").iterdir())


def test_failed_rollback_reports_final_binding_and_keeps_journal(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    k = Kernel()
    k.fail |= {"group_node", "bind:e1000e", "probe"}
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError) as caught:
        binder.bind()
    message = str(caught.value)
    assert "rollback failed" in message and "driver is none" in message
    assert binder.final_driver is None
    assert not k.locked  # lock released after the recovery attempt
    # The next session refuses to touch the device until someone checks it.
    k.fail.clear()
    again = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError, match="did not confirm"):
        again.bind()
    assert k.driver is None and not k.locked


def test_preexisting_vfio_is_used_in_place_and_left_bound(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """The review's second scenario: a donor already on vfio-pci used to end
    up with no driver at all."""
    k = Kernel(driver="vfio-pci", override="vfio-pci")
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    with binder:
        assert k.driver == "vfio-pci"
    assert (k.driver, k.override, k.locked) == ("vfio-pci", "vfio-pci", False)
    assert binder.final_driver == "vfio-pci"


def test_unbind_failure_is_raised_with_actual_binding(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    k = Kernel()
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    binder.bind()
    k.fail |= {"bind:e1000e", "probe"}
    with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError, match="driver is none"):
        binder.unbind()
    assert not k.locked
    assert any((tmp_path / "j").iterdir())  # incident survives for next session


def test_foreign_driver_is_not_touched(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    k = Kernel()
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    binder.bind()
    k.driver = "nouveau"  # someone else rebound it meanwhile
    with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError, match="left untouched"):
        binder.unbind()
    assert k.driver == "nouveau"


def test_override_restore_failure_is_reported(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    k = Kernel()
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    binder.bind()
    k.fail.add("restore_override")
    with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError, match="driver_override was not restored"):
        binder.unbind()
    assert not k.locked


def test_without_journal_directory_no_files_are_written(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    k = Kernel()
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch)
    with binder:
        pass
    assert k.driver == "e1000e"


def test_mismatched_original_override_is_restored(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """driver X with override Y. X must be bound with the override
    cleared, then Y put back; restoring Y first makes the kernel refuse X."""
    k = Kernel(driver="e1000e", override="vfio-pci")
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    with binder:
        assert k.driver == "vfio-pci"
    assert (k.driver, k.override) == ("e1000e", "vfio-pci")


def test_preexisting_vfio_with_empty_override_is_not_given_one(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """a device on vfio-pci via ids= has no override; restore must not
    invent one (which then fails its own verification)."""
    k = Kernel(driver="vfio-pci", override="")
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    binder.bind()
    k.driver = None  # e.g. something unbound it during the session
    binder.unbind()
    assert (k.driver, k.override) == ("vfio-pci", "")


def test_leftover_dynamic_id_is_reported_when_binding_fails(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """a failed remove_id lets drivers_probe hand the device back to
    vfio-pci; the error must say why."""
    k = Kernel()
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    binder.bind()
    k.fail |= {"remove_id", "bind:e1000e"}
    with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError) as caught:
        binder.unbind()
    assert "driver is vfio-pci" in str(caught.value)
    assert "remove_id 8086:1533 failed" in str(caught.value)


def test_permission_error_does_not_skip_remaining_steps(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """every restore step is attempted and the result verified."""
    from pcileechfwgenerator.exceptions import VFIOPermissionError

    k = Kernel()
    binder = binder_for(k, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
    binder.bind()
    unbind = binder._unbind_driver

    def denied():
        raise VFIOPermissionError("denied")

    monkeypatch.setattr(binder, "_unbind_driver", denied)
    with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError, match="unbind vfio-pci: denied"):
        binder.unbind()
    assert binder.final_driver == "vfio-pci"  # verified and reported
    monkeypatch.setattr(binder, "_unbind_driver", unbind)


def test_rebinding_a_reused_binder_does_not_restore_a_stale_driver(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """original_driver is re-read on every bind(); a device with no
    driver now must not inherit the previous session's driver."""
    from types import SimpleNamespace

    monkeypatch.setattr(VFIOBinder, "_validate_permissions", staticmethod(lambda: None))
    monkeypatch.setattr(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context", lambda self: None)
    binder = VFIOBinder(BDF, attach=False, journal_directory=None)
    binder.original_driver = "e1000e"  # from an earlier bind()
    binder._path_manager = SimpleNamespace(driver_path=tmp_path / "no-driver")
    binder._save_original_driver()
    assert binder.original_driver is None


def test_every_binder_journals_by_default(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """ConfigSpaceManager's binder (no explicit directory) journals too."""
    from pcileechfwgenerator.host_collect.register_learning import JOURNAL_DIR_ENV

    monkeypatch.setenv(JOURNAL_DIR_ENV, str(tmp_path / "host"))
    monkeypatch.setattr(VFIOBinder, "_validate_permissions", staticmethod(lambda: None))
    monkeypatch.setattr(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context", lambda self: None)
    binder = VFIOBinder(BDF, attach=False)
    assert binder._journal_directory == tmp_path / "host" / "bindings"
    assert (
        VFIOBinder(BDF, attach=False, journal_directory=None)._journal_directory is None
    )
```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unit tests for the VFIO constants module.

This test suite ensures that all VFIO constants are properly defined,
have correct values, and that the module can be imported without errors.
"""

import ctypes

import pytest

from pcileechfwgenerator.cli.vfio_constants import (VFIO_CHECK_EXTENSION,
                                    VFIO_DEVICE_GET_REGION_INFO,
                                    VFIO_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH,
                                    VFIO_GET_API_VERSION,
                                    VFIO_GROUP_FLAGS_CONTAINER_SET,
                                    VFIO_GROUP_FLAGS_VIABLE,
                                    VFIO_GROUP_GET_DEVICE_FD,
                                    VFIO_GROUP_GET_STATUS,
                                    VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER,
                                    VFIO_REGION_INFO_FLAG_MMAP,
                                    VFIO_REGION_INFO_FLAG_READ,
                                    VFIO_REGION_INFO_FLAG_WRITE,
                                    VFIO_SET_IOMMU, VFIO_TYPE,
                                    VFIO_TYPE1_IOMMU, VfioGroupStatus,
                                    VfioRegionInfo, vfio_group_status,
                                    vfio_region_info)


class TestVFIOConstants:
    """Test suite for VFIO constants."""

    def test_vfio_device_name_max_length_defined(self):
        """Test that VFIO_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH is defined and has a reasonable value."""
        assert VFIO_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH is not None
        assert isinstance(VFIO_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH, int)
        assert VFIO_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH > 0
        assert VFIO_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH <= 512  # Reasonable upper bound

    def test_vfio_type_constant(self):
        """Test that VFIO_TYPE is properly defined."""
        assert VFIO_TYPE == ord(";")
        assert isinstance(VFIO_TYPE, int)

    def test_vfio_iommu_constants(self):
        """Test VFIO IOMMU related constants."""
        assert VFIO_TYPE1_IOMMU == 1
        assert isinstance(VFIO_TYPE1_IOMMU, int)

    def test_vfio_region_flags(self):
        """Test VFIO region info flags."""
        assert VFIO_REGION_INFO_FLAG_READ == (1 << 0)
        assert VFIO_REGION_INFO_FLAG_WRITE == (1 << 1)
        assert VFIO_REGION_INFO_FLAG_MMAP == (1 << 2)

    def test_vfio_group_flags(self):
        """Test VFIO group flags."""
        assert VFIO_GROUP_FLAGS_VIABLE == (1 << 0)
        assert VFIO_GROUP_FLAGS_CONTAINER_SET == (1 << 1)

    def test_ioctl_constants_are_integers(self):
        """Test that all IOCTL constants are integers."""
        ioctl_constants = [
            VFIO_GET_API_VERSION,
            VFIO_CHECK_EXTENSION,
            VFIO_SET_IOMMU,
            VFIO_GROUP_GET_STATUS,
            VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER,
            VFIO_GROUP_GET_DEVICE_FD,
            VFIO_DEVICE_GET_REGION_INFO,
        ]

        for const in ioctl_constants:
            assert isinstance(const, int)
            assert const > 0

    def test_vfio_structures_defined(self):
        """Test that VFIO structures are properly defined."""
        # Test vfio_group_status
        assert hasattr(vfio_group_status, "_fields_")
        assert len(vfio_group_status._fields_) == 2

        status = vfio_group_status()
        assert hasattr(status, "argsz")
        assert hasattr(status, "flags")

        # Test vfio_region_info
        assert hasattr(vfio_region_info, "_fields_")
        assert len(vfio_region_info._fields_) == 6

        region = vfio_region_info()
        assert hasattr(region, "argsz")
        assert hasattr(region, "flags")
        assert hasattr(region, "index")
        assert hasattr(region, "cap_offset")
        assert hasattr(region, "size")
        assert hasattr(region, "offset")

    def test_legacy_aliases(self):
        """Test that legacy aliases are properly defined."""
        assert VfioGroupStatus is vfio_group_status
        assert VfioRegionInfo is vfio_region_info

    def test_structure_sizes(self):
        """Test that structures have expected sizes."""
        # vfio_group_status should have 2 uint32 fields = 8 bytes
        status = vfio_group_status()
        assert ctypes.sizeof(status) == 8

        # vfio_region_info should have 4 uint32 + 2 uint64 fields = 32 bytes
        region = vfio_region_info()
        assert ctypes.sizeof(region) == 32

    def test_ioctl_encoding(self):
        """Test that IOCTL values are encoded correctly."""
        # VFIO_GET_API_VERSION should be _IO(VFIO_TYPE, 0)
        # This is a basic sanity check that the encoding produces non-zero values
        assert VFIO_GET_API_VERSION != 0

        # Check that different IOCTLs have different values
        ioctl_values = {
            VFIO_GET_API_VERSION,
            VFIO_CHECK_EXTENSION,
            VFIO_SET_IOMMU,
            VFIO_GROUP_GET_STATUS,
            VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER,
            VFIO_GROUP_GET_DEVICE_FD,
            VFIO_DEVICE_GET_REGION_INFO,
        }
        assert len(ioctl_values) == 7  # All values should be unique

    def test_module_imports_without_errors(self):
        """Test that the module can be imported without any errors."""
        # This test passes if we get here without import errors
        import pcileechfwgenerator.cli.vfio_constants

        assert pcileechfwgenerator.cli.vfio_constants is not None

    def test_all_exports(self):
        """Test that __all__ exports are properly defined."""
        from pcileechfwgenerator.cli import vfio_constants

        # Check that __all__ is defined
        assert hasattr(vfio_constants, "__all__")
        assert isinstance(vfio_constants.__all__, list)

        # Check that all exported names exist
        for name in vfio_constants.__all__:
            assert hasattr(
                vfio_constants, name
            ), f"Exported name '{name}' not found in module"

        # Check that VFIO_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH is in exports
        assert "VFIO_DEVICE_NAME_MAX_LENGTH" in vfio_constants.__all__

    def test_constants_are_hardcoded_not_computed(self):
        """Test that constants are hardcoded values, not computed at runtime."""
        # Read the source file and check for hardcoded values vs computed ones
        import inspect
        import os

        # Get the path to the vfio_constants module
        import pcileechfwgenerator.cli.vfio_constants as vfio_constants

        source_file = inspect.getfile(vfio_constants)

        with open(source_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            content = f.read()

        # Check that we have hardcoded constants section
        assert (
            "extracted from kernel headers at build time" in content
            or "VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER =" in content
        ), "Constants should be hardcoded, not computed"

        # Verify critical constants are integers, not function calls
        assert isinstance(VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER, int)
        assert isinstance(VFIO_GET_API_VERSION, int)
        assert isinstance(VFIO_SET_IOMMU, int)

    def test_constants_values_are_reasonable(self):
        """Test that VFIO constants have reasonable values."""
        # VFIO constants should be in a reasonable range for ioctl numbers
        # Typically Linux ioctl numbers are 32-bit values
        constants_to_check = [
            VFIO_GET_API_VERSION,
            VFIO_CHECK_EXTENSION,
            VFIO_SET_IOMMU,
            VFIO_GROUP_GET_STATUS,
            VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER,
            VFIO_GROUP_GET_DEVICE_FD,
            VFIO_DEVICE_GET_REGION_INFO,
        ]

        for const in constants_to_check:
            # Should be positive integers
            assert isinstance(const, int)
            assert const > 0
            # Should fit in 32-bit range
            assert const < 2**32
            # Should be reasonable ioctl values (typically > 1000)
            assert const > 1000

    def test_errno_25_causing_constants_fixed(self):
        """Test that constants known to cause errno 25 are properly defined."""
        # The specific constant that was causing errno 25 (ENOTTY)
        # VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER is the one mentioned in the error logs

        # It should be a hardcoded integer, not a computed value
        assert isinstance(VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER, int)

        # It should have a reasonable value for a Linux ioctl constant
        # Linux ioctl values are 32-bit constants that can be quite large
        # The value 0x40043b04 (1074019076) is the correct VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER value
        assert VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER > 0
        assert VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER < 2**32  # Should fit in 32-bit range

        # Verify other critical constants as well
        critical_constants = {
            "VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER": VFIO_GROUP_SET_CONTAINER,
            "VFIO_SET_IOMMU": VFIO_SET_IOMMU,
            "VFIO_GET_API_VERSION": VFIO_GET_API_VERSION,
        }

        for name, value in critical_constants.items():
            assert isinstance(value, int), f"{name} should be hardcoded integer"
            assert value > 0, f"{name} should be positive"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pytest.main([__file__, "-v"])
```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
VFIO Container Hardening Tests.

Tests for container-specific VFIO hardening features:
- Inter-process locking
- Device node waiting
- Aggressive remove_id cleanup
- SELinux/AppArmor diagnostics
"""

import fcntl
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, Mock, patch

import pytest
from pcileechfwgenerator.cli.vfio_handler import VFIOBinder
from pcileechfwgenerator.exceptions import VFIOBindError, VFIOGroupError


class TestVFIOContainerHardening:
    """Test container-specific VFIO hardening features."""

    @pytest.fixture
    def valid_bdf(self):
        """Valid BDF for testing."""
        return "0000:01:00.0"

    @pytest.fixture
    def mock_vfio_environment(self):
        """Mock a complete VFIO environment."""
        with (
            patch("os.geteuid", return_value=0),
            patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=True),
            patch("pathlib.Path.read_text", return_value="0x10de\n"),
            patch("pathlib.Path.write_text"),
            patch("pathlib.Path.resolve") as mock_resolve,
        ):

            # Mock IOMMU group path resolution
            mock_group_path = Mock()
            mock_group_path.name = "42"
            mock_resolve.return_value = mock_group_path

            yield

    def test_wait_for_group_node_success(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test successful wait for group device node."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)

            # Mock device node appearing immediately
            with patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=True):
                # Should not raise
                binder._wait_for_group_node("42", timeout=1.0)

    def test_wait_for_group_node_timeout(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test timeout waiting for group device node."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)

            # Mock device node never appearing
            with patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=False):
                with pytest.raises(VFIOGroupError, match="Timeout waiting"):
                    binder._wait_for_group_node("42", timeout=0.1)

    def test_wait_for_group_node_delayed(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test wait for group node that appears after delay."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)

            # Mock device node appearing after 2 checks
            call_count = {"value": 0}

            def delayed_exists(self):
                call_count["value"] += 1
                return call_count["value"] > 2

            with patch("pathlib.Path.exists", delayed_exists):
                # Should succeed after delay
                binder._wait_for_group_node("42", timeout=1.0)
                assert call_count["value"] > 2

    def test_acquire_group_lock_success(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test successful group lock acquisition."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)

            mock_file = MagicMock()
            mock_file.fileno.return_value = 42

            with (
                patch("builtins.open", return_value=mock_file),
                patch("fcntl.flock") as mock_flock,
                patch("pathlib.Path.mkdir"),
            ):

                binder._acquire_group_lock("42")

                # Verify lock acquired
                assert binder._group_lock is not None
                mock_flock.assert_called_once_with(42, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)

    def test_acquire_group_lock_already_locked(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test handling of already locked group."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)

            mock_file = MagicMock()
            mock_file.fileno.return_value = 42

            with (
                patch("builtins.open", return_value=mock_file),
                patch("fcntl.flock", side_effect=OSError("Resource unavailable")),
                patch("pathlib.Path.mkdir"),
            ):

                with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError, match="already in use"):
                    binder._acquire_group_lock("42")

                # Verify file was closed
                mock_file.close.assert_called_once()

    def test_release_group_lock(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test group lock release."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)

            mock_file = MagicMock()
            mock_file.fileno.return_value = 42
            binder._group_lock = mock_file

            with patch("fcntl.flock") as mock_flock:
                binder._release_group_lock()

                # Verify unlock and close
                mock_flock.assert_called_once_with(42, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
                mock_file.close.assert_called_once()
                assert binder._group_lock is None

    def test_release_group_lock_handles_errors(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test group lock release handles errors gracefully."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)

            mock_file = MagicMock()
            mock_file.fileno.return_value = 42
            mock_file.close.side_effect = OSError("Close failed")
            binder._group_lock = mock_file

            # Should not raise, just log warning
            binder._release_group_lock()

            # Lock should be cleared even on error
            assert binder._group_lock is None

    def test_cleanup_device_ids_single_id(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):

    def test_cleanup_device_ids_handles_errors(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test cleanup handles errors without raising."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)
            binder._added_device_ids = [("10de", "1234")]

            with (
                patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=True),
                patch("pathlib.Path.write_text", side_effect=OSError("Write failed")),
            ):

                # Should not raise; the failure is reported, and the ID is
                # kept so it can be retried (a leftover dynamic ID makes
                # vfio-pci claim the device on the next probe).
                failures = binder._cleanup_device_ids()

                assert failures and "remove_id 10de:1234 failed" in failures[0]
                assert binder._added_device_ids == [("10de", "1234")]

                # Verify lock was released

    def test_unbind_cleans_up_device_ids(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test that unbind() cleans up device IDs."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)
            binder._bound = True
            binder._added_device_ids = [("10de", "1234")]

            cleanup_called = {"value": False}

            def mock_cleanup():
                cleanup_called["value"] = True
                binder._added_device_ids.clear()

            with (
                patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=False),
                patch("pathlib.Path.is_symlink", return_value=False),
                patch.object(binder, "_cleanup_device_ids", mock_cleanup),
                patch.object(binder, "_release_group_lock"),
            ):

                # The mocked sysfs cannot confirm the restored binding, so
                # unbind() now reports it instead of claiming success.
                with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError, match="not restored"):
                    binder.unbind()

                # Verify cleanup was called
                assert cleanup_called["value"]

    def test_unbind_releases_lock(self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment):
        """Test that unbind() releases group lock."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)
            binder._bound = True

            lock_released = {"value": False}

            def mock_release():
                lock_released["value"] = True

            with (
                patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=False),
                patch("pathlib.Path.is_symlink", return_value=False),
                patch.object(binder, "_cleanup_device_ids"),
                patch.object(binder, "_release_group_lock", mock_release),
            ):

                # Unverifiable in the mocked sysfs: the lock is released anyway.
                with pytest.raises(VFIOBindError, match="not restored"):
                    binder.unbind()

                # Verify lock was released
                assert lock_released["value"]

    def test_context_manager_exit_cleans_up_on_success(
        self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment
    ):
        """Test context manager cleanup on successful exit."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)
            binder._bound = True
            binder._added_device_ids = [("10de", "1234")]

            cleanup_called = {"value": False}
            lock_released = {"value": False}

            def mock_cleanup():
                cleanup_called["value"] = True
                binder._added_device_ids.clear()

            def mock_release():
                lock_released["value"] = True

            with (
                patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=False),
                patch("pathlib.Path.is_symlink", return_value=False),
                patch.object(binder, "_cleanup_device_ids", mock_cleanup),
                patch.object(binder, "_release_group_lock", mock_release),
            ):

                binder.__exit__(None, None, None)

                # Verify both cleanup and lock release
                assert cleanup_called["value"]
                assert lock_released["value"]

    def test_context_manager_exit_cleans_up_on_error(
        self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment
    ):
        """Test context manager cleanup even when unbind fails."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)
            binder._bound = True
            binder._added_device_ids = [("10de", "1234")]

            cleanup_called = {"value": False}
            lock_released = {"value": False}

            def mock_cleanup():
                cleanup_called["value"] = True
                binder._added_device_ids.clear()

            def mock_release():
                lock_released["value"] = True

            with (
                patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=True),
                patch("pathlib.Path.write_text", side_effect=OSError("Unbind failed")),
                patch.object(binder, "_cleanup_device_ids", mock_cleanup),
                patch.object(binder, "_release_group_lock", mock_release),
            ):

                # Exit should handle the error and still clean up
                binder.__exit__(None, None, None)

                # Verify cleanup happened despite unbind failure
                assert cleanup_called["value"]
                assert lock_released["value"]

    def test_bind_to_vfio_does_not_add_dynamic_ids(
        self, valid_bdf, mock_vfio_environment
    ):
        """Test that _bind_to_vfio tracks added device IDs."""
        with patch.object(VFIOBinder, "_check_security_context"):
            binder = VFIOBinder(valid_bdf, attach=False, journal_directory=None)

            with (
                patch("pathlib.Path.exists", return_value=True),
                patch("pathlib.Path.write_text") as write_text,
                patch("pathlib.Path.read_text", return_value="0x10de\n"),
                patch.object(
                    binder._path_manager,
                    "get_vendor_device_id",
                    return_value=("10de", "1234"),
                ),
            ):

                try:
                    binder._bind_to_vfio()
                except VFIOBindError:
                    # Binding verification will fail, but we just want to check
                    # that IDs were tracked
                    pass

                # new_id is no longer used: driver_override suffices, and
                # new_id would make vfio-pci claim every identical device.
                assert binder._added_device_ids == []
                written = [str(c.args[0]) for c in write_text.call_args_list]
                assert not any("10de 1234" in w for w in written)
```

```py
import importlib
import json
import sys

from pathlib import Path

import pytest


MODULE_NAME = 'scripts.vfio_container_manager'


def load_module(monkeypatch, tmp_path, extra_env=None):
    extra_env = extra_env or {}
    monkeypatch.delenv('PCILEECH_VFIO_STATE_DIR', raising=False)
    for key, value in extra_env.items():
        monkeypatch.setenv(key, value)
    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    sys.path.insert(0, str(repo_root))
    state_dir_value = extra_env.get('PCILEECH_VFIO_STATE_DIR', tmp_path / 'state')
    state_dir = Path(state_dir_value)
    monkeypatch.setenv('PCILEECH_VFIO_STATE_DIR', str(state_dir))
    sys.modules.pop(MODULE_NAME, None)
    return importlib.import_module(MODULE_NAME)


def test_resolve_state_dir_uses_override(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    override = tmp_path / 'custom' / 'vfio'
    module = load_module(
        monkeypatch,
        tmp_path,
        {'PCILEECH_VFIO_STATE_DIR': str(override)},
    )
    assert module.STATE_DIR == override
    assert override.exists()


def test_resolve_state_dir_permission_fallback(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    sys.modules.pop(MODULE_NAME, None)

    temp_dir = tmp_path / 'temp'
    temp_dir.mkdir()
    monkeypatch.delenv('PCILEECH_VFIO_STATE_DIR', raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setenv('XDG_STATE_HOME', str(tmp_path / 'xdg'))
    monkeypatch.setattr(Path, 'home', classmethod(lambda cls: tmp_path / 'home'))

    import scripts.vfio_container_manager as vcm

    original_mkdir = Path.mkdir
    temp_state = temp_dir / 'pcileech-vfio-state'
    fallback_state = Path.cwd() / '.pcileech-vfio-state'

    def fake_mkdir(self, parents=False, exist_ok=False):
        path_str = str(self)
        if path_str.startswith(str(temp_state)):
            return original_mkdir(self, parents=parents, exist_ok=exist_ok)
        if path_str.startswith(str(fallback_state)):
            return original_mkdir(self, parents=parents, exist_ok=exist_ok)
        raise PermissionError('denied')

    monkeypatch.setattr(Path, 'mkdir', fake_mkdir, raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setattr(vcm.tempfile, 'gettempdir', lambda: str(temp_dir))

    module = importlib.reload(vcm)
    assert module.STATE_DIR == temp_state


def test_bind_device_writes_state(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    module = load_module(monkeypatch, tmp_path)

    captured_instances = []

    

    class DummyBinder:
        def __init__(self, bdf, attach=True):
            self.bdf = bdf
            self.attach = attach
            self.original_driver = 'ixgbe'
            captured_instances.append(self)

        def get_device_info(self):
            return module.DeviceInfo(
                bdf=self.bdf,
                vendor_id='1234',
                device_id='5678',
                iommu_group='55',
                driver='',
                description='',
            )

        def bind(self):
            self.bound = True

    monkeypatch.setattr(module, 'VFIOBinder', DummyBinder)

    manager = module.VFIOContainerManager()
    manager.state = {'devices': {}, 'containers': {}}

    group = manager.bind_device('0000:01:00.0')

    assert group == '55'
    assert captured_instances[0].bound is True
    assert '0000:01:00.0' in manager.state['devices']

    saved = json.loads(module.CONTAINER_STATE_FILE.read_text())
    assert '0000:01:00.0' in saved['devices']


def test_unbind_device_removes_state(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    module = load_module(monkeypatch, tmp_path)

    created = []

    

    class DummyBinder:
        def __init__(self, bdf, attach=True):
            self.bdf = bdf
            self.attach = attach
            created.append(self)

        def unbind(self):
            self.unbound = True

    monkeypatch.setattr(module, 'VFIOBinder', DummyBinder)

    manager = module.VFIOContainerManager()
    manager.state = {
        'devices': {
            '0000:02:00.0': {
                'original_driver': 'ixgbe',
                'iommu_group': '66',
            }
        },
        'containers': {},
    }
    manager._save_state()

    assert manager.unbind_device('0000:02:00.0') is True
    assert created[0].unbound is True
    assert '0000:02:00.0' not in manager.state['devices']

    saved = json.loads(module.CONTAINER_STATE_FILE.read_text())
    assert '0000:02:00.0' not in saved['devices']
```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unit tests for VFIO decision logic."""

import os

import pytest
from pathlib import Path

from pcileechfwgenerator.utils.vfio_decision import (
    VFIODecision,

)


class TestVFIODecision:
    """Test VFIODecision dataclass."""

    def test_vfio_decision_enabled(self):
        """Test VFIODecision when enabled."""
        decision = VFIODecision(
            enabled=True,
            reasons=["VFIO available and enabled"],
            context="enabled"
        )
        assert decision.enabled is True
        assert "VFIO available" in decision.reasons[0]
        assert decision.context == "enabled"

    def test_vfio_decision_disabled(self):
        """Test VFIODecision when disabled."""
        decision = VFIODecision(
            enabled=False,
            reasons=["VFIO disabled by environment"],
            context="explicitly_disabled"
        )
        assert decision.enabled is False
        assert "disabled" in decision.reasons[0]
        assert decision.context == "explicitly_disabled"
```
